title.zh: 卷三十一 志第二十一 五行二
title.raw: 卷三十一 志第二十一 五行二 Volume 31 Treatises 21: Five Elements 2

sentences.zh: }}五行傳曰：「好戰攻，輕百姓，飾城郭，侵邊境，則金不從革。

translations.literal: The Tradition of the Five Elements says: "If one is fond of warfare and aggression, slighting the common people, adorning city walls, and encroaching on borderlands, then metal will not follow reform."
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition of the Five Elements states: "When the ruler loves war and attack, treats the people lightly, lavishes ornament on walls and ramparts, and violates the frontier, metal loses its power to be reformed."

sentences.zh: 謂金失其性而為災也。

translations.literal: This means metal loses its nature and becomes a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: That is, metal abandons its proper nature and disaster follows.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「言之不從，是謂不乂。

translations.literal: " It also says: "If words are not heeded, this is called lack of order."
translations.idiomatic: " It further says: "When counsel goes unheeded, that is called failure to govern."

sentences.zh: 厥咎僭，厥罰恒暘，厥極憂。

translations.literal: Its fault is overstepping; its punishment is constant drought; its ultimate limit is sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The fault is presumption; the penalty is unending drought; the extreme is grief.

sentences.zh: 時則有詩妖，時則有介蟲之孽，時則有犬禍，時則有口舌之痾，時則有白眚、白祥。

translations.literal: At such times there are poetic prodigies; at such times calamities of armored insects; at such times canine disasters; at such times diseases of tongue and mouth; at such times white disasters and white portents.
translations.idiomatic: In such seasons one finds ominous verses, plagues of shelled insects, canine calamities, disorders of speech, and white disasters and white omens.

sentences.zh: 惟木沴金。

translations.literal: Only wood harms metal.
translations.idiomatic: Wood alone is what afflicts metal.

sentences.zh: 」介蟲，劉歆傳以為毛蟲。

translations.literal: " Armored insects—in Liu Xin's tradition are taken to be hairy creatures.
translations.idiomatic: " As for armored insects, Liu Xin's tradition interprets them as hairy creatures.

sentences.zh: 金不從革

translations.literal: Metal not following reform
translations.idiomatic: Metal Fails to Follow Reform

sentences.zh: 魏世張掖石瑞，雖是晉氏之浮命，而於魏為妖。

translations.literal: In the Wei era the stone auspice of Zhangye, though it was the floating destiny of the Jin house, was for Wei an omen of ill.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wei, the stone portent at Zhangye—though it foretold the Jin dynasty's rise—was an evil omen for Wei itself.

sentences.zh: 好攻戰，輕百姓，飾城郭，侵邊境，魏氏三祖皆有其事。

translations.literal: Fondness for attack and warfare, slighting the people, adorning walls and cities, encroaching on borders—the three founders of Wei all had these in their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Love of war, neglect of the people, ornamented fortifications, and border raids—all three Wei founders were guilty of these.

sentences.zh: 劉歆以為金石同類，石圖發非常之文，此不從革之異也。

translations.literal: Liu Xin held that metal and stone are of the same category; the stone diagram issued extraordinary writing—this is the anomaly of not following reform.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin regarded metal and stone as kindred; when a stone chart bore extraordinary inscriptions, that was the prodigy of metal failing to follow reform.

sentences.zh: 晉定大業，多敝曹氏，石瑞文「大討曹」之應也。

translations.literal: When Jin settled the great enterprise, it largely overthrew the Cao house; the stone auspice's text "great campaign against Cao" was the corresponding proof.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin secured the empire and brought down the house of Cao, the inscription on the stone—"a great punitive expedition against Cao"—was the fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝青龍中，盛修宮室，西取長安金狄，承露槃折，聲聞數十里，金狄泣，於是因留霸城。

translations.literal: In the Qinglong era of Emperor Ming of Wei, when palace construction was lavish, they took the golden figure from Chang'an in the west; the Dew-Receiving Basin broke, the sound heard for several tens of li; the golden figure wept, and so it was left at Bacity.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming of Wei, in the Qinglong period, as palaces were built on a grand scale, the golden statue was brought from Chang'an in the west; the Dew Basin snapped with a crash heard for miles, and the statue was said to weep—so it was left behind at Bacity.

sentences.zh: 此金失其性而為異也。

translations.literal: This is metal losing its nature and becoming an anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: This was metal abandoning its nature and turning into a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 吳時，歷陽縣有巖穿似印，咸云「石印封發，天下太平」。

translations.literal: In Wu times, in Liyang County a rock bore a hole like a seal; all said, "When the stone seal opens, the realm will be at peace."
translations.idiomatic: During Wu, at Liyang County a cliff face bore a mark like a seal, and everyone said, "When the stone seal breaks open, the empire will be at peace."

sentences.zh: 孫晧天璽元年印發。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi of Sun Hao, the seal opened.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Sun Hao's Tianxi reign, the seal opened.

sentences.zh: 又陽羨山有石穴，長十餘丈。

translations.literal: Also at Mount Yangxian there was a stone cavern more than ten zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Yangxian there was also a stone cavern over ten zhang in length.

sentences.zh: 晧初修武昌宮，有遷都之意。

translations.literal: When Hao first repaired the Wuchang Palace, he had the intention of moving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao first rebuilt the Wuchang Palace, he intended to move the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時武昌為離宮。

translations.literal: At that time Wuchang served as a detached palace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wuchang functioned as a secondary palace.

sentences.zh: 班固云：「離宮與城郭同占。

translations.literal: Ban Gu said: "Detached palaces share the same prognostication as city walls."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu wrote: "Detached palaces fall under the same omen category as city walls and ramparts."

sentences.zh: 」飾城郭之謂也。

translations.literal: " This is what is meant by adorning walls and cities.
translations.idiomatic: " That is the sense of "adorning city walls."

sentences.zh: 寶鼎三年，晧出東關，遣丁奉至合肥；

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, Hao went out through the eastern pass and sent Ding Feng to Hefei;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoding, Hao marched out through the eastern pass and dispatched Ding Feng to Hefei;

sentences.zh: 建衡三年，晧又大舉出華里。

translations.literal: in the third year of Jianheng, Hao again mounted a major campaign out of Huali.
translations.idiomatic: and in the third year of Jianheng he launched another major expedition from Huali.

sentences.zh: 侵邊境之謂也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by encroaching on the borders.
translations.idiomatic: These were instances of encroaching on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 故令金失其性，卒面縛而吳亡。

translations.literal: Therefore metal lost its nature; in the end he was bound and Wu perished.
translations.idiomatic: Thus metal lost its proper nature; in the end he was brought before his enemies in bonds, and Wu was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永興元年，成都伐長沙，每夜戈戟鋒有火光如縣燭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxing of Emperor Hui of Jin, when Chengdu attacked Changsha, each night the tips of spears and halberds had firelight like suspended candles.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongxing under Emperor Hui of Jin, as Chengdu campaigned against Changsha, every night the points of spears and halberds glowed like torches hung in the air.

sentences.zh: 此輕民命，好攻戰，金失其性而為變也。

translations.literal: This is slighting the people's lives, fondness for warfare—metal losing its nature and becoming a transformation.
translations.idiomatic: This signified contempt for human life and love of war—metal had lost its nature and changed form.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，兵猶火也，不戢將自焚。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: arms are like fire; if not checked, they will burn oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seemed to say: armies are like fire—if you do not restrain them, you will be consumed.

sentences.zh: 成都不悟，終以敗亡。

translations.literal: Chengdu did not understand; in the end it was defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu took no heed and was ultimately ruined.

sentences.zh: 晉懷帝永嘉元年，項縣有魏豫州刺史賈逵石碑，生金可采。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongjia of Emperor Huai of Jin, at Xiang County there was the stone stele of Jia Kui, Inspector of Yuzhou under Wei; gold grew on it and could be mined.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongjia under Emperor Huai of Jin, at Xiang County the stele of Jia Kui, former Inspector of Yuzhou for Wei, sprouted gold that could be gathered.

sentences.zh: 此金不從革而為變也。

translations.literal: This is metal not following reform and becoming a transformation.
translations.idiomatic: This was metal failing to follow reform and changing its nature.

sentences.zh: 五月，汲桑作亂，羣寇飈起。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Ji Sang raised rebellion and bandits rose like a whirlwind.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Ji Sang rebelled, and marauders swept across the land.

sentences.zh: 晉清河王覃為世子時，所佩金鈴忽生起如粟者。

translations.literal: When Prince Qinghe Sima Tan was heir apparent, on the gold bell he wore something suddenly grew like millet grains.
translations.idiomatic: While Prince Qinghe Sima Tan was still heir apparent, on the gold bell at his belt something suddenly sprouted, grain by grain like millet.

sentences.zh: 康王母疑不祥，毀棄之。

translations.literal: The mother of Emperor Kang doubted it was auspicious and destroyed and discarded it.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, the consort of Emperor Kang, took it for a bad omen and had it destroyed.

sentences.zh: 及後為惠帝太子，不終于位，卒為司馬越所殺。

translations.literal: Later when he became heir to Emperor Hui, he did not complete his position; in the end he was killed by Sima Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he became heir to Emperor Hui, he never finished his tenure and was eventually killed by Sima Yue.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝永昌元年，甘卓將襲王敦，既而中止。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang of Emperor Yuan of Jin, Gan Zhuo was about to attack Wang Dun, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchang under Emperor Yuan of Jin, Gan Zhuo prepared to strike Wang Dun, then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 及還家，多變怪，照鏡不見其頭。

translations.literal: When he returned home, many strange transformations occurred; looking in a mirror he could not see his head.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned home, uncanny things multiplied; when he looked in a mirror, his head was not there.

sentences.zh: 此金失其性而為妖也。

translations.literal: This is metal losing its nature and becoming an evil omen.
translations.idiomatic: This was metal losing its nature and turning into a portent of doom.

sentences.zh: 尋為敦所襲，遂夷滅。

translations.literal: Before long he was attacked by Dun and utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Dun struck him down, and he and his house were exterminated.

sentences.zh: 石虎時，鄴城鳳陽門上金鳳皇二頭，飛入漳河。

translations.literal: In the time of Shi Hu, the two golden phoenixes atop the Fengyang Gate of Ye City flew into the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shi Hu, the pair of golden phoenixes on the Fengyang Gate at Ye City flew off into the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 晉海西太和中，會稽山陰縣起倉，鑿地得兩大船，滿中錢，錢皆輪文大形。

translations.literal: In the Tahe era of Emperor Haixi of Jin, at Shanyin County in Kuaiji they built a granary; digging the ground they obtained two large boats full of cash, all coins with large wheel patterns.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tahe reign of Emperor Haixi of Jin, when Shanyin County in Kuaiji built a granary, excavators uncovered two great boats packed with coins, each bearing large ring-shaped rims.

sentences.zh: 時日向莫，鑿者馳以告官。

translations.literal: The sun was then near dusk; the diggers galloped to report to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: The day was nearly done; the workmen raced to inform the magistrate.

sentences.zh: 官夜遣防守甚嚴。

translations.literal: The officials sent guards by night with great strictness.
translations.idiomatic: That night the authorities posted a heavy guard.

sentences.zh: 至明旦，失錢所在，唯有船存，視其狀，悉有錢處。

translations.literal: By dawn the coins were gone from where they had been; only the boats remained, and looking at their form, every place that had held coins was evident.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the money had vanished; only the empty boats remained, their hulls still showing where the coins had lain.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙初，東陽太守殷仲文照鏡不見其頭，尋亦誅翦，占與甘同。

translations.literal: In the early Yixi era of Emperor An of Jin, the Administrator of Dongyang Yin Zhongwen looked in a mirror and could not see his head; before long he too was executed—the omen matched Gan Zhuo's case.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yixi era under Emperor An of Jin, Yin Zhongwen, Administrator of Dongyang, looked into a mirror and saw no head; he too was soon executed—the same omen as Gan Zhuo's.

sentences.zh: 宋後廢帝元徽四年，義熙、晉陵二郡，並有霹靂車墜地，如青石，草木燋死。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhui of the deposed Emperor of Song, in the two commanderies of Yixi and Jinling, thunder chariots fell to earth like bluestone; grass and trees were scorched dead.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhui under the deposed Liu-Song emperor, in both Yixi and Jinling commanderies thunder-wagons crashed to earth like masses of green stone, and vegetation was burned black.

sentences.zh: 言之不從

translations.literal: Words not heeded
translations.idiomatic: Words Not Heeded

sentences.zh: 魏齊王嘉平初，東郡有譌言云，白馬河出妖馬，夜過官牧邊嗚呼，眾馬皆應。

translations.literal: In the early Jiaping era of the Qi King of Wei, in Dong Commandery there was a rumor saying that from the White Horse River came a demon horse; at night passing the government pasture it neighed, and all the horses answered.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiaping era of Cao Wei's Qi-king, Dong Commandery circulated a saying that a demon horse had come forth from the White Horse River; at night it passed the imperial stud and whinnied, and every horse answered.

sentences.zh: 明日見其迹，大如斛，行數里，還入河。

translations.literal: The next day its tracks were seen, large as a hu measure; it went several li and returned into the river.
translations.idiomatic: The next day its tracks were found, each print as large as a grain measure; it had gone several li and gone back into the river.

sentences.zh: 楚王彪本封白馬，兗州刺史令狐愚以彪有智勇，及聞此言，遂與王淩謀共立之。

translations.literal: Prince of Chu Biao was originally enfeoffed at White Horse; the Inspector of Yanzhou Linghu Yu, because Biao had wisdom and courage, upon hearing this saying joined with Wang Ling in a plot to enthrone him together.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Biao of Chu had originally been enfeoffed at White Horse; Yanzhou Inspector Linghu Yu, judging Biao intelligent and brave, and hearing this rumor, joined Wang Ling in a plot to set him on the throne.

sentences.zh: 遣人謂曰：「天下事未可知，願王自愛。

translations.literal: He sent someone to say to him: "The affairs of the realm are not yet knowable; may Your Highness take care for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: He sent a message: "The empire's fate is still uncertain; I pray that Your Highness guard your own person."

sentences.zh: 」彪答曰：「知厚意。

translations.literal: " Biao replied: "I know your generous intent."
translations.idiomatic: " Biao replied: "I understand your kindness."

sentences.zh: 」事泄，淩、愚被誅，彪賜死。

translations.literal: " The affair leaked out; Ling and Yu were executed, and Biao was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: " When the plot was exposed, Ling and Yu were executed, and Biao was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 此言不從之罰也。

translations.literal: This is the punishment for words not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for words going unheeded.

sentences.zh: 詩云：「民之譌言，寧莫之懲。」

translations.literal: The Odes say: "The people's rumors—will none be punished?"
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Poetry says: "When the people spread rumors, is there no one to check them?"

sentences.zh: 劉禪嗣位，譙周引晉穆侯、漢靈帝命子事譏之曰：「先主諱備，其訓具也。

translations.literal: When Liu Shan succeeded the throne, Qiao Zhou cited the cases of Duke Mu of Jin and Emperor Ling of Han naming their heirs to mock him, saying: "The late lord's taboo name Bei, its gloss is 'complete.'"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shan took the throne, Qiao Zhou cited how Duke Mu of Jin and Emperor Ling of Han had named their heirs, and mocked him: "The late lord's taboo name Bei means 'complete.'"

sentences.zh: 後主諱禪，其訓授也。

translations.literal: "The later lord's taboo name Shan, its gloss is 'hand over.'"
translations.idiomatic: "The present lord's taboo name Shan means 'to hand over.'"

sentences.zh: 若言劉已具矣，當授與人，甚於穆侯、靈帝之祥也。

translations.literal: "If one says the Liu house is already complete, and should be handed to another, this is an omen more telling than those of Duke Mu and Emperor Ling."
translations.idiomatic: "If Liu is already complete and must be handed to someone else, the omen is clearer than those of Duke Mu or Emperor Ling."

sentences.zh: 」蜀果亡，此言之不從也。

translations.literal: " Shu indeed perished—this is words not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu was indeed destroyed—another case of words not heeded.

sentences.zh: 劉備卒，劉禪即位，未葬，亦未踰月，而改元為建興。

translations.literal: When Liu Bei died, Liu Shan took the throne; before burial, and not yet a full month, he changed the era name to Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei died, Liu Shan ascended before the burial and before a month had passed changed the era name to Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 此言之不從也。

translations.literal: This is words not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: This too was a case of words not heeded.

sentences.zh: 習鑿齒曰：「禮，國君即位踰年而後改元者，緣臣子之心，不忍一年而有二君也。

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi said: "By ritual, when a state's lord succeeds, he changes the era name only after a full year—because in the hearts of ministers and subjects they cannot bear to have two lords in one year."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi wrote: "By ritual a ruler changes the era name only after a full year in office, because subjects cannot bear to acknowledge two sovereigns within a single year."

sentences.zh: 今可謂亟而不知禮矣。

translations.literal: "Now one may say he was hasty and ignorant of ritual."
translations.idiomatic: "Here was haste combined with ignorance of ritual."

sentences.zh: 君子是以知蜀之不能東遷也。

translations.literal: "The gentleman therefore knew that Shu could not move east and recover."
translations.idiomatic: "From this the wise knew that Shu could never march east and reclaim the empire."

sentences.zh: 」後又降晉。

translations.literal: "Later it again submitted to Jin."
translations.idiomatic: "Later it surrendered to Jin."

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮、晉惠帝、宋元凶亦然。

translations.literal: Sun Liang of Wu, Emperor Hui of Jin, and the deposed Yuan of Song were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang of Wu, Emperor Hui of Jin, and the deposed Yuan of Liu Song did the same.

sentences.zh: 亮不終其位，惠帝號令非己，元凶尋誅。

translations.literal: Liang did not complete his position; Hui's orders were not his own; the deposed Yuan was soon executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liang never finished his reign; Hui's commands were not his own; the deposed Yuan was soon put to death.

sentences.zh: 言不從也。

translations.literal: Words not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: In each case, words had not been heeded.

sentences.zh: 魏太和中，姜維歸蜀，失其母。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era of Wei, Jiang Wei returned to Shu and lost his mother.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Taihe era, when Jiang Wei went back to Shu, his mother was left behind.

sentences.zh: 魏人使其母手書呼維令反，并送當歸以譬之。

translations.literal: The people of Wei had his mother write by hand calling Wei to return, and also sent the herb danggui as a parable.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei authorities had his mother write urging him to come back, and sent the herb danggui—"should return"—as a pun.

sentences.zh: 維報書曰：「良田百頃，不計一畝。

translations.literal: Wei replied in a letter: "A hundred qing of good fields—one mu is not counted."
translations.idiomatic: Wei wrote back: "A hundred qing of fertile fields—and not one mu is counted."

sentences.zh: 但見遠志，無有當歸。

translations.literal: "I only see yuanzhi; there is no danggui."
translations.idiomatic: "I see only yuanzhi—'far ambition'—and no danggui—'must return.'"

sentences.zh: 」維卒不免。

translations.literal: "In the end Wei could not escape disaster."
translations.idiomatic: "In the end Wei could not escape his fate."

sentences.zh: 魏明帝景初元年，有司奏帝為烈祖，與太祖、高祖並為不毀之廟。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingchu of Emperor Ming of Wei, the relevant offices memorialized to honor the emperor as Liezu, together with Taizu and Gaozu establishing temples that would never be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingchu, Emperor Ming of Wei's officials proposed enshrining him as Liezu alongside Taizu and Gaozu in temples that would never be removed.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: He followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was accepted.

sentences.zh: 按宗廟之制，祖宗之號，皆身沒名成，乃正其禮。

translations.literal: According to the system of ancestral temples, the titles of ancestors and founders are all fixed only after death when the name is established, and then ritual is corrected.
translations.idiomatic: By the rules of the ancestral temple, honorific temple names are fixed only after death, when merit is known, and only then is ritual made correct.

sentences.zh: 故雖功赫天壤，德邁前王，未有豫定之典。

translations.literal: Therefore even if merit shines between heaven and earth and virtue surpasses former kings, there is no precedent for predetermining the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Thus even for merit that fills heaven and earth and virtue that eclipses earlier kings, there was no precedent for settling the rites in advance.

sentences.zh: 此蓋言之不從，失之甚者也。

translations.literal: This is probably words not heeded—a very great error.
translations.idiomatic: This was counsel gone unheeded—a grave breach of propriety.

sentences.zh: 後二年而宮車晏駕，於是統微政逸。

translations.literal: Two years later the imperial carriage passed peacefully; thereafter the lineage weakened and governance lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the emperor died, and thereafter the imperial line weakened and government drifted.

sentences.zh: 吳孫休世，烏程民有得困疾，及差，能以響言者，言於此而聞於彼。

translations.literal: In the reign of Sun Xiu of Wu, a man of Wucheng who had suffered confining illness, when recovered could use echo speech—speaking here and being heard there.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Xiu of Wu, a man of Wucheng who had been bedridden with a wasting illness recovered with the power of "resonant speech"—words spoken in one place heard in another.

sentences.zh: 自其所聽之，不覺其聲之大也；

translations.literal: From where he listened, one did not notice how loud the sound was;
translations.idiomatic: To the listener nearby, the voice did not seem loud;

sentences.zh: 自遠聽之，如人對言，不覺聲之自遠來也。

translations.literal: from far away listening, it was like people speaking face to face, not noticing that the sound came from afar.
translations.idiomatic: but heard from afar it was like conversation face to face, with no sense that the voice had traveled any distance.

sentences.zh: 聲之所往，隨其所向，遠者不過十數里。

translations.literal: Where the sound went followed where it was directed; at most it did not exceed a dozen or so li.
translations.idiomatic: The voice went wherever he aimed it, but no farther than ten-odd li.

sentences.zh: 其鄰人有責息於外，歷年不還。

translations.literal: A neighbor of his had a debt owed from outside that for years was not repaid.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor had money owed him from afar that for years had not been returned.

sentences.zh: 乃假之使為責讓，懼以禍福，負物者以為鬼神，即傾倒畀之。

translations.literal: He therefore borrowed him to make demands for repayment, frightening with fortune and disaster; the debtor thought it was spirits and immediately poured out everything and gave it.
translations.idiomatic: The neighbor borrowed his gift to demand repayment, threatening fortune or ruin; the debtor took it for the work of spirits and at once paid everything he owed.

sentences.zh: 其人亦不自知所以然也。

translations.literal: That person also did not himself know why it was so.
translations.idiomatic: Even the man with the power did not understand how it worked.

sentences.zh: 言不從之咎也。

translations.literal: This is the fault of words not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for words not heeded.

sentences.zh: 魏世起安世殿，晉武帝後居之。

translations.literal: In the Wei era the Anshi Hall was built; Emperor Wu of Jin later dwelt in it.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei the Anshi Hall was erected; Emperor Wu of Jin later lived there.

sentences.zh: 安世，武帝字也。

translations.literal: Anshi was Emperor Wu's style name.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was Emperor Wu's courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝每延羣臣，多說平生常事，未嘗及經國遠圖。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Wu of Jin received the ministers, he mostly spoke of ordinary matters from his life, never touching on governing the state or far-reaching plans.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Wu of Jin entertained his ministers, he talked mostly of everyday matters from his past and never of statecraft or long-range design.

sentences.zh: 此言之不從也。

translations.literal: This is words not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: This was another case of words not heeded.

sentences.zh: 何曾謂子遵曰：「國家無貽厥之謀，及身而已，後嗣其殆乎，此子孫之憂也。

translations.literal: He Zeng said to his son Zun: "The state has no plans to leave to posterity—it lasts only for one's own person; the later generations are probably in peril—this is the worry of sons and grandsons."
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng told his son Zun: "The realm has no plans bequeathed to posterity—only what serves the present. Our descendants are in peril; that is a father's worry."

sentences.zh: 」自永熙後，王室漸亂。

translations.literal: "From after Yongxi, the royal house gradually fell into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: "After the Yongxi era the imperial house slowly unraveled."

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，天下大壞。

translations.literal: "In the Yongjia era, the realm was greatly ruined."
translations.idiomatic: "In the Yongjia years the empire collapsed."

sentences.zh: 及何綏以非辜被誅，皆如曾言。

translations.literal: "When He Sui was executed without crime, all was as Zeng had said."
translations.idiomatic: "When He Sui was executed though innocent, everything came to pass as Zeng had foretold."

sentences.zh: 趙王倫廢惠帝於金墉城，改號金墉為永安宮。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Lun deposed Emperor Hui at Jincheng and changed the name of Jincheng to Yong'an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun of Zhao deposed Emperor Hui at the Jincheng compound and renamed it the Palace of Eternal Peace.

sentences.zh: 帝尋復位而倫誅。

translations.literal: The emperor soon regained the throne and Lun was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was soon restored, and Lun was put to death.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永興元年，詔廢太子覃還為清河王，立成都王穎為皇太弟，猶加侍中，大都督，領丞相，備九錫，封二十郡，如魏王故事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxing of Emperor Hui of Jin, an edict deposed the heir Tan and returned him to Prince of Qinghe, establishing Prince of Chengdu Ying as Imperial Younger Brother, still adding Palace Attendant, Grand Commander, leading Chancellor, complete with the Nine Bestowals, enfeoffing twenty commanderies, following the precedent of the King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongxing, Emperor Hui deposed Crown Prince Tan and made him Prince of Qinghe again, while elevating Prince Ying of Chengdu as Imperial Younger Brother—with Palace Attendant, Grand Commander, and Chancellor, the full Nine Bestowals, and twenty commanderies, on the model of Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 案周禮，傳國以胤不以勳，故雖公旦之聖，不易成王之嗣。

translations.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou, transmitting the state relies on the heir, not on merit; therefore even the sage Duke of Zhou did not replace the heir of King Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou prescribe that the realm passes by lineal descent, not by merit; even the Duke of Zhou, for all his wisdom, did not displace King Cheng's heir.

sentences.zh: 所以遠絕覬覦，永壹宗祧。

translations.literal: By this means covetous gazes are kept far away and the ancestral line is forever unified.
translations.idiomatic: That is how ambition is held at bay and the imperial line kept one.

sentences.zh: 後代遵履，改之則亂。

translations.literal: Later generations followed and trod this path; to change it brings disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages followed this rule; to alter it was to invite chaos.

sentences.zh: 今擬非其實，僭差已甚。

translations.literal: Now the plan does not match reality; the overstepping is already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: The present arrangement bore no relation to proper practice; presumption had gone very far.

sentences.zh: 且既為國副，則不應復開封土，兼領庶職。

translations.literal: Moreover, once one is deputy to the state, one should not again receive enfeoffed lands or concurrently hold numerous offices.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, once he was heir to the realm, he ought not also to receive territorial fiefs or pile up concurrent posts.

sentences.zh: 此言之不從，進退乖爽。

translations.literal: This is words not heeded—advance and retreat at odds.
translations.idiomatic: This was counsel unheeded, with advance and retreat wholly at odds.

sentences.zh: 故帝既播越，穎亦不終，是其咎也。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperor was driven into exile and Ying also did not finish—this was its fault.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the emperor was driven from his capital and Ying likewise came to no good end—the penalty for it.

sentences.zh: 後猶不悟，又立懷帝為皇太弟。

translations.literal: Later they still did not understand, and again established Emperor Huai as Imperial Younger Brother.
translations.idiomatic: They still took no lesson and again made Emperor Huai Imperial Younger Brother.

sentences.zh: 懷終流弒，不永厥祚，又其應也。

translations.literal: Huai in the end was driven into exile and assassinated, his reign not long-lasting—again the corresponding proof.
translations.idiomatic: Huai was ultimately driven out and murdered, his reign cut short—again the fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「變古易常，不亂則亡。

translations.literal: A saying goes: "To change the ancient and alter the constant—if not disorder, then destruction."
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says: "Change what is old and alter what is fixed—if it does not bring chaos, it brings ruin."

sentences.zh: 」此之謂乎。

translations.literal: " Is this not what is meant?"
translations.idiomatic: " Was this not the case?"

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝太安中，周玘於陽羨起宅，始成，而邊戶有聲如人嘆咤者。

translations.literal: In the Taian era of Emperor Hui of Jin, Zhou Qi built a residence at Yangxian; when it was first completed, at the side doors there were sounds like people sighing and exclaiming.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taian years under Emperor Hui of Jin, Zhou Qi built a house at Yangxian; as soon as it was finished, voices like human sighs and cries were heard at the side doors.

sentences.zh: 玘亡後，家誅滅。

translations.literal: After Qi died, the family was executed to the last.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi's death his entire house was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 此近言不從也。

translations.literal: This closely resembles words not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: This was a near instance of words not heeded.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興四年，吳郡民訛言有大蟲在紵中及樗樹上，嚙人即死。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan of Jin, the people of Wu Commandery spread a rumor that a great insect was in ramie plants and ailanthus trees; if it bit a person, he died at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan of Jin, Wu Commandery was rife with rumors of a great insect in ramie thickets and ailanthus trees that killed anyone it bit.

sentences.zh: 晉陵民又言曰，見一老女子居市，被髮從肆人乞飲，自言：「天帝令我從水門出，而我誤由蟲門。

translations.literal: The people of Jinling also said they saw an old woman in the market, hair unbound, begging drink from shopkeepers, saying herself: "The Lord on High ordered me to go out by the Water Gate, but I mistakenly went by the Insect Gate."
translations.idiomatic: In Jinling people also claimed to have seen an old woman in the market with loose hair begging drink from shopkeepers, who said: "Heaven commanded me to leave by the Water Gate, but I wrongly took the Insect Gate."

sentences.zh: 若還，天帝必殺我。

translations.literal: "If I return, the Lord on High will surely kill me."
translations.idiomatic: "If I go back, Heaven will surely kill me."

sentences.zh: 如何？

translations.literal: "What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: "What am I to do?"

sentences.zh: 」於是百姓共相恐動，云死者已十數也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the common people mutually frightened one another, saying the dead already numbered more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: " The populace panicked one another, claiming that more than ten had already died.

sentences.zh: 西及京都，諸家有樗紵者，伐去之。

translations.literal: Westward to the capital, every household with ailanthus or ramie cut them down.
translations.idiomatic: The panic spread west to the capital; every household that had ailanthus or ramie cut them down.

sentences.zh: 無幾自止。

translations.literal: Before long it stopped of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the uproar ceased on its own.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝永昌元年，寧州刺史王遜遣子澄入質，將渝、濮雜夷數百人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang of Emperor Yuan of Jin, the Inspector of Ningzhou Wang Xun sent his son Cheng as hostage, bringing several hundred mixed Yi of Yu and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchang, Ningzhou Inspector Wang Xun sent his son Cheng to court as a hostage, accompanied by several hundred mixed tribesmen from Yu and Pu.

sentences.zh: 京邑民忽訛言寧州人大食人家小兒，親有見其蒸煮滿釜甑中者。

translations.literal: The people of the capital suddenly spread a rumor that men of Ningzhou greatly ate people's small children; some personally saw them steaming them full in pots and steamers.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the capital was rife with rumors that Ningzhou men were eating people's children, with eyewitnesses who claimed to have seen them steaming children by the potful.

sentences.zh: 又云失兒皆有主名，婦人尋道，拊心而哭。

translations.literal: They also said every lost child had a named owner, and women searched the roads, beating their breasts and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: They also said each missing child had a known owner, and women searched the streets beating their breasts and wailing.

sentences.zh: 於是百姓各禁錄小兒，不得出門。

translations.literal: Thereupon the common people each locked up their small children, not allowing them to go out.
translations.idiomatic: Parents everywhere locked their children indoors and forbade them to go out.

sentences.zh: 尋又言已得食人之主，官當大航頭大杖考竟。

translations.literal: Before long they again said the master who ate people had been obtained; the officials would at the great ferry landing beat him to death with large staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they added that the man-eater had been caught and that officials would beat him to death with heavy staves at the great ferry landing.

sentences.zh: 而日有四五百人晨聚航頭，以待觀行刑。

translations.literal: Each day four or five hundred people gathered at dawn at the ferry to wait and watch the execution.
translations.idiomatic: Every morning four or five hundred people gathered at the ferry to watch the execution.

sentences.zh: 朝廷之士相問者，皆曰信然，或言郡縣文書已上。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen asking one another all said it was true; some said the commandery and county documents had already been submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When court officials asked one another, all said it was true; some said the local reports had already reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 王澄大懼，檢測之，事了無形，民家亦未嘗有失小兒者，然後知其訛言也。

translations.literal: Wang Cheng was greatly afraid and investigated; the affair had absolutely no substance, and civilian households also had never lost small children—only then did they know it was a false rumor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng was terrified and investigated; nothing was found, and no household had actually lost a child—only then was it recognized as mere rumor.

sentences.zh: 此二事，干寶云「未之能論」。

translations.literal: Of these two affairs, Gan Bao said, "I have not been able to discuss them."
translations.idiomatic: Of these two incidents Gan Bao wrote that he "could not yet explain them."

sentences.zh: 永昌二年，大將軍王敦下據姑孰。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchang, the Grand General Wang Dun descended and held Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongchang Grand General Wang Dun seized Gushu.

sentences.zh: 百姓訛言行蟲病，食人大孔，數日入腹，入腹則死。

translations.literal: The people spread a rumor of traveling insect disease: it ate people at a large hole; in several days it entered the belly, and entering the belly one died.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread of a traveling insect plague that ate people through a large hole, entered the belly within days, and killed once inside.

sentences.zh: 治之有方，當得白犬膽以為藥。

translations.literal: There was a method to treat it: one must obtain the gall of a white dog as medicine.
translations.idiomatic: There was said to be a cure: the gall of a white dog.

sentences.zh: 自淮、泗遂及京都，數日之間，百姓驚擾，人人皆自云已得蟲病。

translations.literal: From the Huai and Si it reached the capital; within several days the common people were alarmed and disturbed, every person saying he had already contracted the insect disease.
translations.idiomatic: From the Huai and Si regions to the capital, within days the populace was in uproar, everyone claiming to have the insect disease.

sentences.zh: 又云，始在外時，當燒鐵以灼之。

translations.literal: They also said that when it was first outside the body, one should burn iron to cauterize it.
translations.idiomatic: They also said that while the insect was still outside the body, one should burn iron and cauterize the spot.

sentences.zh: 於是翕然被燒灼者十七八矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon all at once those who were burned numbered seven or eight out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly seven or eight out of ten were being burned.

sentences.zh: 而白犬暴貴，至相請奪，其價十倍。

translations.literal: White dogs suddenly became extremely expensive, to the point of mutual begging and seizing; their price increased tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: White dogs soared in price tenfold, with buyers fighting over them.

sentences.zh: 或有自云能行燒鐵者，賃灼百姓，日得五六萬，憊而後已。

translations.literal: Some who claimed they could perform iron-burning hired themselves out to cauterize the common people, earning fifty or sixty thousand a day, and only stopped when exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Men who claimed skill at iron cautery hired themselves out to burn the afflicted, earning fifty or sixty thousand a day until they could work no more.

sentences.zh: 四五日漸靜。

translations.literal: In four or five days it gradually quieted.
translations.idiomatic: Within four or five days the panic subsided.

sentences.zh: 說曰，夫裸蟲人類，而人為之主，今云蟲食人，言本同臭類而相殘賊也。

translations.literal: The explanation says: naked creatures are the human kind, yet humans are their masters; now it is said insects eat people—meaning those of the same kind by nature yet mutually harming and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: The interpretation runs: mankind belongs to the class of naked creatures and rules over it; to say insects devour men is to say that those of the same kind destroy one another.

sentences.zh: 自下而上，斯其逆也。

translations.literal: From below attacking upward—this is its rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Striking from below upward—that is rebellion.

sentences.zh: 必入腹者，言害由中不由外也。

translations.literal: "Must enter the belly" means the harm comes from within, not from without.
translations.idiomatic: That it must enter the belly means the harm arises from within, not from without.

sentences.zh: 犬有守禦之性，白者金色，而膽用武之主也。

translations.literal: Dogs have a nature of guarding and defense; white is the color of metal, and gall is used by the lord of military force.
translations.idiomatic: Dogs are creatures of defense; white belongs to metal, and gall is the remedy ruled by the agent of war.

sentences.zh: 帝王之運，五霸會於戌，戌主用兵。

translations.literal: The fortune of emperors and kings—the Five Hegemons gather at the branch xu; xu governs the use of arms.
translations.idiomatic: In the cycles of imperial fortune the Five Hegemons converge at the xu branch, which governs warfare.

sentences.zh: 金者晉行，火燒鐵以治疾者，言必去其類而來，火與金合德，共治蟲害也。

translations.literal: Metal is the element of Jin; burning iron with fire to treat the disease means one must remove its kind and come—fire and metal combine in virtue to together govern the insect calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Metal is Jin's element; burning iron to treat the disease means the hostile kind must be driven out—fire and metal join in power to quell the plague together.

sentences.zh: 案中興之際，大將軍本以腹心受伊、呂之任，而元帝末年，遂攻京邑，明帝諒闇，又有異謀。

translations.literal: Examining the time of the Restoration, the Grand General originally received the trust of a bosom companion with the charge of Yi Yin and Lü Shang, yet in the late years of Emperor Yuan he attacked the capital; Emperor Ming was young and in mourning, and there was again a divergent plot.
translations.idiomatic: At the Restoration the Grand General had been trusted like Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou, yet in Emperor Yuan's last years he attacked the capital; when Emperor Ming was a child in mourning, rebellion brewed again.

sentences.zh: 是以下逆上，腹心內爛也。

translations.literal: Therefore subordinates rebelled against superiors—the belly and heart rotted within.
translations.idiomatic: Hence rebellion from below and corruption at the heart.

sentences.zh: 及錢鳳、沈充等逆兵四合，而為王師所挫，踰月而不能濟。

translations.literal: When Qian Feng, Shen Chong, and others' rebel armies gathered from four sides yet were checked by the royal army, more than a month passed without success.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel armies of Qian Feng and Shen Chong converged from all sides yet were beaten back by the imperial forces, more than a month passed without victory.

sentences.zh: 北中郎將劉遐及淮陵內史蘇峻率淮、泗之眾以救朝廷，故其謠言首作於淮、泗也。

translations.literal: North General of the Household Liu Xia and Interior Minister of Huailing Su Jun led the masses of the Huai and Si to rescue the court; therefore the rumor first arose in the Huai and Si.
translations.idiomatic: North General of the Household Liu Xia and Huailing Interior Minister Su Jun led Huai-Si troops to rescue the court—hence the rumor first appeared in the Huai and Si regions.

sentences.zh: 朝廷卒以弱制強，罪人授首，是用白犬膽可救之效也。

translations.literal: The court in the end used the weak to control the strong; the guilty man surrendered his head—this is the efficacy by which white dog's gall could save.
translations.idiomatic: The court ultimately overcame the strong with the weak and took the rebel leaders' heads—the effect for which white dog's gall was the symbol.

sentences.zh: 晉海西時，庾晞四五年中，喜為挽歌，自搖大鈴為唱，使左右齊和。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Haixi of Jin, within four or five years Yu Xi delighted in funeral dirges, himself shaking a great bell as he sang, making attendants join in chorus.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Haixi of Jin, for four or five years Yu Xi loved to sing funeral dirges, ringing a great bell himself while his attendants joined the chorus.

sentences.zh: 又燕會，輒令倡妓作新安人歌儛離別之辭，其聲悲切。

translations.literal: At banquets he always ordered singing girls to perform the Xin'an people's song and dance of parting words, its sound mournful and piercing.
translations.idiomatic: At feasts he would have entertainers perform the Xin'an parting song and dance, its notes piercingly sad.

sentences.zh: 時人怪之，後亦果敗。

translations.literal: People of the time thought it strange; later he indeed met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries found it ominous, and he was indeed ruined afterward.

sentences.zh: 晉海西公太和以來，大家婦女，緩鬢傾髻，以為盛飾。

translations.literal: From the Taihe era of Emperor Haixi of Jin, great families' women wore loose side-locks and slanting topknots as grand adornment.
translations.idiomatic: From the Taihe reign of Emperor Haixi onward, ladies of great houses wore loose side-locks and slanting chignons as high fashion.

sentences.zh: 用髮既多，不恒戴。

translations.literal: Using hair was already abundant, so they did not constantly wear it.
translations.idiomatic: They used so much hair that they could not always wear their own.

sentences.zh: 乃先作假髻，施於木上，呼曰「假頭」。

translations.literal: They therefore first made false chignons, placed on wood, calling them "false heads."
translations.idiomatic: They made false chignons mounted on frames and called them "false heads."

sentences.zh: 人欲借，名曰「借頭」。

translations.literal: When people wished to borrow them, they were called "borrowed heads."
translations.idiomatic: To borrow one was to ask for a "borrowed head."

sentences.zh: 遂布天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon they spread throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The fashion spread across the empire.

sentences.zh: 自此以來，人士多離事故，或亡失頭首，或以草木為之。

translations.literal: From this time, gentlemen often parted from their affairs through death, some losing their actual heads, some making them of grass and wood.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter many men were separated from life by death, some losing their real heads, some making do with grass and wood.

sentences.zh: 假頭之言，此其先兆也。

translations.literal: The words "false head"—this was its omen beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: The talk of "false heads" was the omen beforehand.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武太元中，立內殿名曰清暑，少時而崩。

translations.literal: In the Taixuan era of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, an inner hall was established named Clear Summer; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taixuan years of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin an inner hall called Clear Summer was built, and soon afterward the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 時人曰，「清暑」者，反言楚聲也。

translations.literal: People of the time said "Clear Summer" read backward gives the sound of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: People said that read backward "Clear Summer" sounded like "Chu."

sentences.zh: 果有哀楚之聲。

translations.literal: Indeed there was the mournful sound of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: And indeed there came the mournful note of Chu.

sentences.zh: 有人曰：「非此之謂，豈可極言乎。

translations.literal: Someone said: "This is not what is meant—how can one speak to the limit?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone objected: "That is not the point—can one really press the omen so far?"

sentences.zh: 讖云，代晉者楚，其在茲乎？

translations.literal: "A prophecy says, 'He who replaces Jin is Chu'—is it here?"
translations.idiomatic: "A prophecy says, 'Chu will replace Jin'—is this it?"

sentences.zh: 」及桓玄篡逆，自號曰楚。

translations.literal: " When Huan Xuan usurped, he styled himself Chu."
translations.idiomatic: " When Huan Xuan seized the throne, he took the style Chu."

sentences.zh: 太元中，小兒以兩鐵相打於土中，名曰「鬭族」。

translations.literal: In the Taixuan era, small boys struck two pieces of iron together in the earth, calling it "clan fighting."
translations.idiomatic: In the Taixuan years boys knocked two iron pieces together in the dirt, calling the game "clan combat."

sentences.zh: 後王國寶、王孝伯一姓之中，自相攻擊也。

translations.literal: Later Wang Guobao and Wang Xiaobo, within one clan, attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Guobao and Wang Xiaobo, of the same clan, turned on each other.

sentences.zh: 桓玄出鎮南州，立齋名曰蟠龍。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan went out to garrison the southern province, he established a studio named Coiled Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan took up his post in the south, he built a studio called Coiled Dragon.

sentences.zh: 後劉毅居此齋。

translations.literal: Later Liu Yi dwelt in this studio.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Yi occupied that studio.

sentences.zh: 蟠龍，毅小字也。

translations.literal: Coiled Dragon was Yi's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Coiled Dragon was Yi's courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 桓玄初改年為大亨，遐邇讙言曰：「二月了。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan first changed the era name to Great Prosperity, far and near rejoiced, saying: "The second month is finished."
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan first changed the era name to Great Prosperity, people far and near joked: "The second month is over."

sentences.zh: 」故義謀以仲春發也。

translations.literal: " Therefore the righteous plot launched in mid-spring.
translations.idiomatic: " Hence the loyalist rising began in the second month.

sentences.zh: 玄篡立，又改年為建始，以與趙王倫同，又易為永始。

translations.literal: When Xuan usurped the throne, he again changed the era to Establishing Beginning, because it was the same as Prince of Zhao Lun's, then changed again to Eternal Beginning.
translations.idiomatic: After usurping the throne Xuan changed the era to Establishing Beginning, then dropped it because it matched Prince Lun's era, and adopted Eternal Beginning.

sentences.zh: 永始，復是王莽受封之年也。

translations.literal: Eternal Beginning was again the year when Wang Mang received his enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Eternal Beginning was again the year in which Wang Mang had received his fief.

sentences.zh: 始徙司馬道子于安成，晉主遜位，出永安宮，封晉主為平固王，琅邪王德文為石陽公，並使住尋陽城。

translations.literal: First Sima Daozi was moved to Ancheng; the Jin ruler abdicated, left Yong'an Palace, was enfeoffed as Prince of Pinggu, the Prince of Langye Dewen as Duke of Shiyang, and both were made to dwell at Xunyang city.
translations.idiomatic: First Sima Daozi was banished to Ancheng; the Jin emperor abdicated and left Yong'an Palace; the emperor was made Prince of Pinggu and the Prince of Langye, Dewen, Duke of Shiyang, both confined at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 識者皆以為言不從之妖也。

translations.literal: Those with insight all regarded it as the evil omen of words not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The knowing all took this for the portent of words not heeded.

sentences.zh: 厥咎僭。

translations.literal: Its fault is overstepping.
translations.idiomatic: The fault was presumption.

sentences.zh: 晉興，何曾薄太官御膳，自取私食，子劭又過之，而王愷又過劭。

translations.literal: When Jin arose, He Zeng slighted the imperial kitchen's meals and took private food; his son Shao went beyond him, and Wang Kai again went beyond Shao.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Jin, He Zeng disdained the imperial kitchen and ate privately; his son Shao outdid him, and Wang Kai outdid Shao.

sentences.zh: 王愷、羊琇之疇，盛致聲色，窮珍極麗。

translations.literal: Wang Kai, Yang Xiu, and their kind lavishly gathered music and beauty, exhausting rare things and extreme splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai, Yang Xiu, and their circle lavished music and courtesans, exhausting every rarity and extravagance.

sentences.zh: 至元康中，夸恣成俗，轉相高尚，石崇之侈，遂兼王、何而儷人主矣。

translations.literal: By the Yuankang era, boasting and indulgence became custom, each surpassing the other in elevation; Shi Chong's extravagance then combined Wang and He and matched the human lord.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yuankang years extravagance had become fashion, each outdoing the next; Shi Chong's luxury surpassed Wang and He together and rivaled the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 崇既誅死，天下尋亦淪喪。

translations.literal: When Chong was executed and died, the realm soon also fell into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: After Chong was executed, the empire soon collapsed.

sentences.zh: 僭踰之咎也。

translations.literal: This is the fault of overstepping and exceeding.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for presumption.

sentences.zh: 恒暘

translations.literal: Constant drought
translations.idiomatic: Constant Drought

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和二年五月，大旱。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Taihe of Emperor Ming of Wei, great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Taihe under Emperor Ming of Wei there was a great drought.

sentences.zh: 元年以來，崇廣宮府之應也。

translations.literal: From the first year onward, this was the corresponding proof of exalting and expanding palaces and offices.
translations.idiomatic: Since the first year of the era this answered to the lavish expansion of palaces and offices.

sentences.zh: 又是春，晉宣帝南禽孟達，置二郡；

translations.literal: Also in this spring, the Emperor Xuan of Jin in the south captured Meng Da and established two commanderies;
translations.idiomatic: That same spring Emperor Xuan of Jin captured Meng Da in the south and established two commanderies;

sentences.zh: 張郃西破諸葛亮，斃馬謖。

translations.literal: Zhang He in the west defeated Zhuge Liang and killed Ma Su.
translations.idiomatic: while Zhang He in the west defeated Zhuge Liang and killed Ma Su.

sentences.zh: 亢陽自大，又其應也。

translations.literal: Excessive yang grew arrogant—again its corresponding proof.
translations.idiomatic: Yang had grown overbearing—again the fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「欲德不用，茲謂張。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yi Tradition says: "Desiring virtue yet not employing it—this is called expansion."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Tradition of the Changes says: "Wishing for virtue but not using it—this is called expansion."

sentences.zh: 厥災荒。

translations.literal: Its disaster is famine.
translations.idiomatic: Its calamity is famine.

sentences.zh: 其旱陰雲不雨，變而赤煙四際。

translations.literal: Its drought: yin clouds do not rain, transforming into red smoke on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Its drought: clouds gather but no rain falls, and red haze spreads on every side.

sentences.zh: 眾出過時，茲謂廣。

translations.literal: The masses go out beyond season—this is called broad.
translations.idiomatic: The people go forth out of season—this is called broad.

sentences.zh: 其旱不生。

translations.literal: Its drought: nothing grows.
translations.idiomatic: Its drought: nothing will grow.

sentences.zh: 上下皆蔽，茲謂隔。

translations.literal: Above and below are all obscured—this is called separation.
translations.idiomatic: Above and below are blocked—this is called separation.

sentences.zh: 其旱天赤三月，時有雹殺飛禽。

translations.literal: Its drought: heaven is red for three months; at times hail kills flying birds.
translations.idiomatic: Its drought: the sky is red for three months, and hail sometimes kills birds in flight.

sentences.zh: 上緣求妃，茲謂僭。

translations.literal: The superior seeks concubines on pretext—this is called overstepping.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler seeks consorts on false pretenses—this is called presumption.

sentences.zh: 其旱三月大溫亡雲。

translations.literal: Its drought: three months of great heat without clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Its drought: three months of fierce heat without a cloud.

sentences.zh: 君高臺府，茲謂犯。

translations.literal: The lord has high terraces and mansions—this is called offense.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler builds high terraces and mansions—this is called violation.

sentences.zh: 陰侵陽。

translations.literal: Yin encroaches on yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin encroaches upon yang.

sentences.zh: 其旱萬物根死，數有火災。

translations.literal: Its drought: the roots of all things die; fires occur repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Its drought: the roots of all things die, and fires break out again and again.

sentences.zh: 庶位踰節，茲謂僭。

translations.literal: Subordinate positions exceed their measure—this is called overstepping.
translations.idiomatic: Inferior ranks overstep their bounds—this is called presumption.

sentences.zh: 其旱澤物枯，為火所傷。」

translations.literal: Its drought: marsh plants wither, injured by fire."
translations.idiomatic: Its drought: plants in the marshes wither, harmed by fire."

sentences.zh: 太和五年三月，自去冬十月至此月不雨，辛巳，大雩。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year of Taihe, from the tenth month of last winter until this month there was no rain; on xinsi day, a great rain prayer ceremony was held.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year of Taihe, no rain had fallen since the tenth month of the previous winter; on the day xinsi a great rain-prayer ceremony was performed.

sentences.zh: 是春，諸葛亮寇天水，晉宣王距卻之，亢陽動眾。

translations.literal: That spring, Zhuge Liang invaded Tianshui; the Emperor Xuan of Jin repelled him—excessive yang, mobilizing the masses.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Zhuge Liang raided Tianshui, and the Emperor Xuan of Jin drove him back—excessive yang and the mobilization of armies.

sentences.zh: 又是時三隅分據，眾出多過時也。

translations.literal: Also at this time the three corners were divided and held separately—the masses going out mostly beyond season.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time the three realms held their separate corners, and armies were sent forth far out of season.

sentences.zh: 春秋說曰：「傷二穀，謂之不雨。」

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Explanatory Tradition says: "When two grain seasons are harmed, it is called no rain."
translations.idiomatic: The Explanatory Tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals states: "When two grain harvests are harmed, that is called failure of rain."

sentences.zh: 魏齊王正始元年二月，自去冬十二月至此月不雨。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Zhengshi of the Qi King of Wei, from the twelfth month of last winter until this month there was no rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Zhengshi under the Qi King of Wei, no rain had fallen since the twelfth month of the previous winter.

sentences.zh: 去歲正月，明帝崩。

translations.literal: In the first month of the previous year, Emperor Ming died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the preceding year Emperor Ming had died.

sentences.zh: 二月，曹爽白嗣主，轉晉宣王為太傅，外示尊崇，內實欲令事先由己。

translations.literal: In the second month, Cao Shuang reported to the successor ruler and transferred the Emperor Xuan of Jin to Grand Tutor—outwardly showing honor, but inwardly truly wishing affairs to go through himself first.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Cao Shuang petitioned the new emperor to make the Emperor Xuan of Jin Grand Tutor—outwardly an honor, but in truth he meant to keep all affairs in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 是時宣王功蓋魏朝，欲德不用之應也。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor Xuan's merit covered the Wei court—the corresponding proof of wishing for virtue but not employing it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor Xuan's achievements overshadowed the Wei court—the fulfillment of wishing for virtue but not employing it.

sentences.zh: 魏高貴鄉公甘露三年正月，自去秋至此月旱。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Ganlu of the Duke of Gaoguixiang of Wei, drought from last autumn until this month.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Ganlu under the Duke of Gaoguixiang of Wei, drought had continued from the previous autumn.

sentences.zh: 時晉文王圍諸葛誕，眾出過時之應也。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor Wen of Jin besieged Zhuge Dan—the corresponding proof of masses going out beyond season.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor Wen of Jin was besieging Zhuge Dan—the fulfillment of armies sent forth out of season.

sentences.zh: 初，壽春秋夏常雨潦，常淹城，而此旱踰年，城陷乃大雨。

translations.literal: Initially, Shou in spring and summer often had rain and floods, often inundating the city—but this drought exceeded a year, and when the city fell, then came great rain.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Shou in spring and summer was often flooded by rain and the city was regularly inundated; yet this drought lasted more than a year, and only when the city fell did heavy rain come.

sentences.zh: 咸以為天亡。

translations.literal: All regarded it as heaven's destruction.
translations.idiomatic: All took it as heaven's decree of destruction.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮五鳳二年，大旱，民饑。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wufeng of Sun Liang of Wu, great drought; the people starved.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wufeng under Sun Liang of Wu there was a great drought, and the people went hungry.

sentences.zh: 是歲閏月，魏將文欽以淮南眾數萬口來奔；

translations.literal: That year in the intercalary month, the Wei general Wen Qin came over with tens of thousands from Huainan;
translations.idiomatic: That year in the intercalary month the Wei general Wen Qin defected with tens of thousands of people from Huainan;

sentences.zh: 孫峻又破魏將曹珍于高亭。

translations.literal: Sun Jun also defeated the Wei general Cao Zhen at Gaoting.
translations.idiomatic: and Sun Jun also defeated the Wei general Cao Zhen at Gaoting.

sentences.zh: 三月，朱異襲安豐，不克。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhu Yi raided Anfeng and did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Zhu Yi attacked Anfeng but failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 七月，城廣陵、東海二郡。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, fortified the two commanderies of Guangling and Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the two commanderies of Guangling and Donghai were walled.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以馮朝為監軍使者，督徐州諸軍，軍士怨叛。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Feng Chao was made military overseer commissioner to supervise all armies of Xuzhou; soldiers resented and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Feng Chao was appointed military overseer commissioner to command the armies of Xuzhou, and the troops mutinied in resentment.

sentences.zh: 此亢陽自大，勞民失眾之罰也。

translations.literal: This was the penalty of excessive yang growing arrogant, toiling the people and losing the masses.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for overbearing yang, exhausting the people and losing their support.

sentences.zh: 其役彌歲，故旱亦竟年。

translations.literal: The labor extended a full year, so the drought also lasted the whole year.
translations.idiomatic: The corvée labor lasted a full year, and so the drought lasted the whole year as well.

sentences.zh: 吳孫晧寶鼎元年春夏旱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding of Sun Hao of Wu, drought in spring and summer.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoding under Sun Hao of Wu there was drought through spring and summer.

sentences.zh: 是時晧遷都武昌，勞民動眾之應也。

translations.literal: At this time Hao moved the capital to Wuchang—the corresponding proof of toiling the people and mobilizing the masses.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hao moved the capital to Wuchang—the fulfillment of exhausting the people and mobilizing armies.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始七年五月閏月，旱，大雩。

translations.literal: In the fifth intercalary month of the seventh year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, drought; great rain prayer ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of the seventh year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin there was drought, and a great rain-prayer ceremony was held.

sentences.zh: 是春，孫晧出華里，大司馬望帥眾次于淮北。

translations.literal: That spring, Sun Hao went out to Huali; the Grand Marshal Wang led forces and encamped north of the Huai River.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Sun Hao marched out to Huali, while the Grand Marshal Wang led his army and encamped north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 四月，北地胡寇金城西平，涼州刺史牽弘出戰，敗沒。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the northern Di and Hu raided Jincheng and Xiping; the Inspector of Liang, Qian Hong, went out to battle and was defeated and lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the northern Di and Hu raided Jincheng and Xiping; the Inspector of Liang, Qian Hong, marched out to fight and was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 泰始八年五月，旱。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Taishi, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Taishi there was drought.

sentences.zh: 是時帝納荀勗邪說，留賈充不復西鎮，而任愷稍疏，上下皆蔽之應也。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor accepted Xun Xu's perverse counsel, kept Jia Chong from returning to western garrison, and Ren Kai was gradually distanced—the corresponding proof of above and below all being obscured.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor heeded Xun Xu's perverse advice, kept Jia Chong from returning to his western post, and gradually distanced Ren Kai—the fulfillment of obstruction above and below.

sentences.zh: 又李憙、魯芝、李胤等並在散職，近欲德不用之謂也。

translations.literal: Also Li Xi, Lu Zhi, Li Yin and others were all in idle posts—closely related to wishing for virtue but not employing it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi, Lu Zhi, Li Yin, and others were also relegated to empty posts—nearly a case of wishing for virtue but not employing it.

sentences.zh: 泰始九年，自正月旱，至于六月，祈宗廟社稷山川，癸未雨。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taishi, drought from the first month until the sixth month; prayed at ancestral temples, altars of soil and grain, and mountains and rivers—on guisi day still no rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taishi drought continued from the first month through the sixth; prayers were offered at the ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, and the mountains and rivers, yet on the day guisi still no rain fell.

sentences.zh: 去年九月，吳西陵督步闡據城來降，遣羊祜統楊肇等眾八萬救迎闡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the previous year, Bu Chan, governor of Xiling in Wu, held the city and came to surrender; Yang Hu was dispatched to command Yang Zhao and others with eighty thousand troops to rescue and welcome Chan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the previous year Bu Chan, governor of Xiling in Wu, held the city and came over to surrender; Yang Hu was sent to lead Yang Zhao and others with eighty thousand men to rescue and receive him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，陸抗大破肇軍，攻闡滅之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Lu Kang greatly defeated Zhao's army, attacked and destroyed Chan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Lu Kang routed Zhao's army and attacked and destroyed Chan.

sentences.zh: 泰始十年四月，旱。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year of Taishi, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year of Taishi there was drought.

sentences.zh: 去年秋冬，采擇卿校諸葛沖等女，是春五十餘人入殿簡選。

translations.literal: Last autumn and winter, daughters of secretaries and commandants including Zhuge Chong were selected; that spring more than fifty entered the palace for selection.
translations.idiomatic: The previous autumn and winter daughters of secretaries and commandants, including Zhuge Chong, were gathered for selection; that spring more than fifty entered the palace to be screened.

sentences.zh: 又取小將吏女數十人，母子號哭於宮中，聲聞于外，行人悲酸。

translations.literal: Also took dozens of daughters of junior officers and officials; mothers and children wailed in the palace, the sound heard outside; passersby were moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of daughters of junior officers and officials were also taken; mothers and daughters wailed inside the palace until the sound carried outside, and passersby were stricken with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 是殆積陰生陽之應也。

translations.literal: This was likely the corresponding proof of accumulated yin giving birth to yang.
translations.idiomatic: This was likely the fulfillment of accumulated yin giving rise to yang.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝咸寧二年五月，旱，大雩，及社稷山川。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Xianning of Emperor Wu of Jin, drought; great rain prayer ceremony, also at altars of soil and grain and mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Xianning under Emperor Wu of Jin there was drought; a great rain-prayer ceremony was held, including at the altars of soil and grain and the mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 至六月，乃澍雨。

translations.literal: By the sixth month, then came soaking rain.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth month soaking rain finally came.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康二年，自去冬旱，至此春平吳，亢陽動眾自大之應也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, drought from last winter; by this spring Wu was pacified—the corresponding proof of excessive yang, mobilizing the masses, and growing arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin drought had continued since the previous winter; by that spring Wu was pacified—the fulfillment of overbearing yang, mass mobilization, and arrogance.

sentences.zh: 太康三年四月，旱。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Taikang, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Taikang there was drought.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔司空齊王攸與尚書、廷尉、河南尹錄訊繫囚，事從蠲宥。

translations.literal: On yiyou day, an edict ordered the Minister of Works Prince of Qi You together with the Masters of Writing, Court Commandant, and Intendant of Henan to review and interrogate imprisoned convicts; cases were to receive leniency and pardon.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiyou an edict ordered the Minister of Works, the Prince of Qi You, together with the Masters of Writing, the Court Commandant, and the Intendant of Henan to review and question prisoners; cases were to be treated with clemency and pardon.

sentences.zh: 太康五年六月，旱。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Taikang, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Taikang there was drought.

sentences.zh: 此年正月，天陰，解而復合。

translations.literal: This year in the first month, the sky was overcast, cleared, then overcast again.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the first month the sky was overcast, then cleared, then clouded over again.

sentences.zh: 劉毅上疏曰：「必有阿黨之臣，姦以事君者，當誅而不赦也。

translations.literal: Liu Yi submitted a memorial saying: "There must be factional ministers who are treacherous in serving the lord—they ought to be executed and not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi submitted a memorial saying: "There must be clique-forming ministers who serve the ruler treacherously—they should be executed without pardon.

sentences.zh: 」帝不答。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor made no reply.

sentences.zh: 是時荀勗、馮紞僭作威福，亂朝尤甚。

translations.literal: At this time Xun Xu and Feng Dan presumptuously wielded power and favor; they disturbed the court especially severely.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xun Xu and Feng Dan presumptuously wielded power and favor, and they especially ravaged the court.

sentences.zh: 太康六年三月，青、涼、幽、冀郡國旱。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year of Taikang, commanderies and principalities of Qing, Liang, You, and Ji had drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year of Taikang the commanderies and principalities of Qing, Liang, You, and Ji suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 太康六年六月，濟陰、武陵旱，傷麥。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Taikang, Jiyin and Wuling had drought, harming wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Taikang Jiyin and Wuling had drought that damaged the wheat crop.

sentences.zh: 太康七年夏，郡國十三旱。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year of Taikang, thirteen commanderies and principalities had drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventh year of Taikang thirteen commanderies and principalities suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 太康八年四月，冀州旱。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year of Taikang, Ji Province had drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year of Taikang Ji Province suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 太康九年夏，郡國三十三旱。

translations.literal: In the summer of the ninth year of Taikang, thirty-three commanderies and principalities had drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the ninth year of Taikang thirty-three commanderies and principalities suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 太康九年六月，扶風、始平、京兆、安定旱，傷麥。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year of Taikang, Fufeng, Shiping, Jingzhao, and Anding had drought, harming wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year of Taikang Fufeng, Shiping, Jingzhao, and Anding had drought that damaged the wheat crop.

sentences.zh: 太康十年二月，旱。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year of Taikang, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the tenth year of Taikang there was drought.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太熙元年二月，旱。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Taixi of Emperor Wu of Jin, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Taixi under Emperor Wu of Jin there was drought.

sentences.zh: 自太康以後，雖正人滿朝，不被親仗；

translations.literal: From Taikang onward, though upright men filled the court, they were not personally relied upon;
translations.idiomatic: From the Taikang era onward, although upright men filled the court, they were not personally trusted;

sentences.zh: 而賈充、荀勗、楊駿、馮紞等，迭居要重。

translations.literal: while Jia Chong, Xun Xu, Yang Jun, Feng Dan and others alternately held crucial positions.
translations.idiomatic: while Jia Chong, Xun Xu, Yang Jun, Feng Dan, and others held one crucial post after another.

sentences.zh: 所以無年不旱者，欲德不用，上下皆蔽，庶位踰節之罰也。

translations.literal: The reason there was drought nearly every year was the penalty of wishing for virtue but not employing it, above and below all being obscured, and subordinate positions exceeding their measure.
translations.idiomatic: The reason drought came nearly every year was the penalty for wishing for virtue but not employing it, for obstruction above and below, and for subordinate ranks overstepping their bounds.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康元年七月，雍州大旱，殞霜疾疫。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, Yong Province had great drought, withering frost and pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin Yong Province suffered great drought, killing frost, and pestilence.

sentences.zh: 關中飢，米斛萬錢。

translations.literal: In Guanzhong there was famine; a hu of rice cost ten thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: In Guanzhong there was famine; a hu of rice cost ten thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 元康七年七月，秦雍二州大旱。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year of Yuankang, the two provinces of Qin and Yong had great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventh year of Yuankang the two provinces of Qin and Yong suffered great drought.

sentences.zh: 故其年氐羌反叛，雍州刺史解系敗績。

translations.literal: Therefore that year the Di and Qiang rebelled; the Inspector of Yong, Xie Xi, was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly that year the Di and Qiang rebelled, and the Inspector of Yong, Xie Xi, was routed.

sentences.zh: 是年正月，周處、盧播等復敗，關西震亂。

translations.literal: That year in the first month, Zhou Chu, Lu Bo and others were again defeated; west of the passes was shaken by disorder.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the first month Zhou Chu, Lu Bo, and others were defeated again, and the region west of the passes was convulsed.

sentences.zh: 交兵彌歲，至是飢疫荐臻，戎、晉並困，朝廷不能振，詔聽相賣鬻。

translations.literal: Fighting each other for a full year, by then famine and pestilence came in succession; Rong and Jin were both exhausted; the court could not restore order and issued an edict permitting mutual buying and selling.
translations.idiomatic: Armies clashed for a full year; by then famine and pestilence came one after another, and both the frontier peoples and Jin were exhausted; the court could not recover, and an edict permitted people to sell one another into bondage.

sentences.zh: 元康七年九月，郡國五旱。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventh year of Yuankang, five commanderies and principalities had drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the seventh year of Yuankang five commanderies and principalities suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永寧元年，自夏及秋，青、徐、幽、并四州旱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongning of Emperor Hui of Jin, from summer through autumn, the four provinces of Qing, Xu, You, and Bing had drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongning under Emperor Hui of Jin drought afflicted the four provinces of Qing, Xu, You, and Bing from summer through autumn.

sentences.zh: 是年春，三王討趙王倫，六旬之中，大小數十戰，死者十餘萬人。

translations.literal: That spring, the three princes campaigned against Prince of Zhao Lun; within sixty days, dozens of battles large and small; over a hundred thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: That spring the three princes marched against the Prince of Zhao, Lun; within sixty days they fought dozens of battles large and small, and more than a hundred thousand men died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，郡國十二又旱。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, twelve commanderies and principalities again had drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month twelve commanderies and principalities again suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 晉懷帝永嘉三年五月，大旱。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Yongjia of Emperor Huai of Jin, great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Yongjia under Emperor Huai of Jin there was a great drought.

sentences.zh: 襄平縣梁水淡淵竭，河、洛、江、漢皆可涉。

translations.literal: In Xiangping county, the Liang River's shallow pools and deep springs dried up; the Yellow, Luo, Yangtze, and Han rivers could all be crossed on foot.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiangping county the Liang River's shallows and deep pools dried up, and the Yellow, Luo, Yangtze, and Han rivers could all be waded across.

sentences.zh: 是年三月，司馬越歸京都，遣兵入宮，收中書令繆播等九人殺之。

translations.literal: That year in the third month, Sima Yue returned to the capital, sent troops into the palace, seized Director of the Secretariat Mi Fu and nine others and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the third month Sima Yue returned to the capital, sent troops into the palace, seized the Director of the Secretariat Mi Fu and nine others, and had them killed.

sentences.zh: 此僭踰之罰也。

translations.literal: This was the penalty for overstepping and exceeding.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for presumption and overstepping.

sentences.zh: 又四方諸侯，多懷無君之心，劉淵、石勒、王彌、李雄之徒，賊害民命，流血成泥，又其應也。

translations.literal: Also the regional lords on all four sides mostly harbored a heart of disloyalty to the lord; Liu Yuan, Shi Le, Wang Mi, Li Xiong and their kind ravaged people's lives, blood flowing like mud—again the corresponding proof.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the lords on all four sides mostly harbored disloyal hearts; Liu Yuan, Shi Le, Wang Mi, Li Xiong, and their kind preyed on the people, and blood flowed like mud—again the fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 永嘉五年，自去冬旱至此春。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongjia, drought from last winter until this spring.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongjia drought continued from the previous winter into that spring.

sentences.zh: 去歲十二月，司馬越棄京都，以大眾南出，多將王公朝士，及以行臺自隨，斥黜禁衞，代以國人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the previous year, Sima Yue abandoned the capital, leading the great host southward, bringing many princes, dukes, and court gentlemen, and taking the mobile imperial secretariat with him; he dismissed the palace guard and replaced them with his countrymen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the previous year Sima Yue abandoned the capital and marched south with a great host, taking many princes, dukes, and court officials with him and bringing the mobile imperial secretariat along; he dismissed the palace guard and replaced them with men of his own domain.

sentences.zh: 宮省蕭然，無復君臣之節矣。

translations.literal: The palace and ministries were desolate—no longer any ritual between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: The palace and ministries stood empty; the rites between ruler and minister were gone.

sentences.zh: 晉陽秋云：「愍帝在西京，旱傷荐臻。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn of Jin says: "The Emperor Min in the Western Capital—drought and injury came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn of Jin says: "The Emperor Min in the Western Capital—drought and disaster came one after another.
