sentences.zh: 」無注記年月也。

translations.literal: " No annotation records the year and month.
translations.idiomatic: " No note records the year and month.

sentences.zh: 晉愍帝建武元年六月，揚州旱。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Jianwu of Emperor Min of Jin, Yang Province had drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Jianwu under Emperor Min of Jin Yang Province suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 去年十二月，淳于伯寃死，其年即旱，而太興元年六月又旱。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the previous year, Chunyu Bo died wrongfully; that year there was drought at once, and in the sixth month of the first year of Taixing there was drought again.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the previous year Chunyu Bo died unjustly; drought came that same year, and in the sixth month of the first year of Taixing there was drought again.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰「殺伯之後旱三年」是也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao says "after killing Bo, drought for three years"—this is that case.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao's remark that "after Bo was killed there was drought for three years" refers to this.

sentences.zh: 案前漢殺孝婦則旱，後漢有囚亦旱，見謝見理，並獲雨澍，此其類也。

translations.literal: Examining: in Former Han when the filial daughter-in-law was killed there was drought; in Later Han a prisoner also brought drought; when wrong was acknowledged and right was seen, both received soaking rain—this is the same type.
translations.idiomatic: Consider: in Former Han drought followed the killing of the filial daughter-in-law; in Later Han a prisoner also brought drought; when the wrong was confessed and justice was seen, both received soaking rain—this is the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 班固曰：「刑罰妄加，羣陰不附，則陽氣勝，故其罰恒暘。

translations.literal: Ban Gu says: "When punishments are wantonly imposed, the multitude of yin does not adhere, then yang qi prevails—therefore its punishment is constant drought.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu says: "When punishments are imposed wantonly, the multitude of yin will not adhere, and yang qi prevails—therefore the penalty is constant drought.

sentences.zh: 」建武元年四月，麴允等悉眾禦寇。

translations.literal: " In the fourth month of the first year of Jianwu, Qu Yun and others led all forces to repel invaders.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth month of the first year of Jianwu Qu Yun and others led all their forces to repel the invaders.

sentences.zh: 五月，祖逖攻譙。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Zu Ti attacked Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zu Ti attacked Qiao.

sentences.zh: 其冬，周訪討杜曾。

translations.literal: That winter, Zhou Fang campaigned against Du Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhou Fang campaigned against Du Zeng.

sentences.zh: 又眾出之應也。

translations.literal: Again the corresponding proof of masses going out.
translations.idiomatic: Again the fulfillment of armies sent forth.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興四年五月，旱。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan of Jin, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan of Jin there was drought.

sentences.zh: 是時王敦強僭之釁漸著。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Dun's omen of forcible presumption gradually became manifest.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the signs of Wang Dun's forcible presumption gradually became clear.

sentences.zh: 又去歲蔡豹、祖逖等，並有征役。

translations.literal: Also in the previous year Cai Bao, Zu Ti and others all had military campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous year as well Cai Bao, Zu Ti, and others had all been on campaign.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝永昌元年，大旱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang of Emperor Yuan of Jin, great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchang under Emperor Yuan of Jin there was a great drought.

sentences.zh: 是年三月，王敦有石頭之變，二宮陵辱，大臣誅死。

translations.literal: That year in the third month, Wang Dun had the Shitou incident; the two palaces suffered humiliation; great ministers were executed.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the third month Wang Dun staged the Shitou coup; the two palaces were humiliated, and great ministers were executed.

sentences.zh: 僭踰無上，故旱尤甚也。

translations.literal: Overstepping without limit—therefore the drought was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Presumption knew no bounds, and so the drought was especially severe.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年閏十一月，京都大旱，川谷並竭。

translations.literal: In the eleventh intercalary month of the first year of Yongchang, the capital had great drought; rivers and valleys all dried up.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month of the first year of Yongchang the capital suffered great drought, and rivers and valleys alike ran dry.

sentences.zh: 晉明帝太寧三年，自春不雨，至于六月。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taining of Emperor Ming of Jin, from spring no rain until the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taining under Emperor Ming of Jin no rain fell from spring until the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 去年秋，滅王敦，亢陽動眾自大之應也。

translations.literal: Last autumn Wang Dun was destroyed—the corresponding proof of excessive yang, mobilizing the masses, and growing arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: The previous autumn Wang Dun was destroyed—the fulfillment of overbearing yang, mass mobilization, and arrogance.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸和元年秋，旱。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng of Jin, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng of Jin there was drought.

sentences.zh: 是時庾太后臨朝稱制，羣臣奏事稱「皇太后陛下」。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Dowager Yu presided at court and claimed regency; ministers presenting affairs addressed her as "Your Majesty the Empress Dowager."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Dowager Yu held court and claimed regency, and ministers presenting business addressed her as "Your Majesty the Empress Dowager."

sentences.zh: 此婦人專王事，言不從而僭踰之罰也。

translations.literal: This was a woman monopolizing royal affairs—a penalty for words not heeded and overstepping and exceeding.
translations.idiomatic: This was a woman monopolizing royal affairs—the penalty for words not heeded and for presumption.

sentences.zh: 與漢鄧太后同事。

translations.literal: The same matter as Empress Dowager Deng of Han.
translations.idiomatic: It was the same case as Empress Dowager Deng of Han.

sentences.zh: 咸和二年夏，旱。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Xianhe, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year of Xianhe there was drought.

sentences.zh: 咸和五年五月，旱。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Xianhe, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Xianhe there was drought.

sentences.zh: 去年殄蘇峻之黨，此春又討郭默滅之。

translations.literal: Last year the faction of Su Jun was exterminated; this spring they also campaigned against Guo Mo and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: The previous year the faction of Su Jun had been exterminated; this spring the court again campaigned against Guo Mo and destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 亢陽動眾之應也。

translations.literal: The corresponding proof of excessive yang and mobilizing the masses.
translations.idiomatic: This was the fulfillment of overbearing yang and mass mobilization.

sentences.zh: 咸和六年四月，旱。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year of Xianhe, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year of Xianhe there was drought.

sentences.zh: 去年八月，石勒遣郭敬寇襄陽，南中郎將周撫奔武昌。

translations.literal: Last year in the eighth month, Shi Le sent Guo Jing to raid Xiangyang; the Southern Palace Gentleman-Commander Zhou Fu fled to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the previous year Shi Le sent Guo Jing to raid Xiangyang, and the Southern Palace Gentleman-Commander Zhou Fu fled to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 十月，李雄使李壽寇建平，建平太守楊謙奔宜都。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Li Xiong sent Li Shou to raid Jianping; the Administrator of Jianping Yang Qian fled to Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Li Xiong sent Li Shou to raid Jianping, and the Administrator of Jianping, Yang Qian, fled to Yidu.

sentences.zh: 此正月，劉徵略婁縣，於是起眾警備。

translations.literal: This first month, Liu Zheng plundered Lou County; therefore troops were raised for emergency defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month Liu Zheng plundered Lou County, whereupon the court mobilized troops for emergency defense.

sentences.zh: 咸和八年七月，旱。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year of Xianhe, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighth year of Xianhe there was drought.

sentences.zh: 咸和九年，自四月不雨，至于八月。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianhe, from the fourth month no rain until the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xianhe no rain fell from the fourth month until the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康元年六月，旱。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Xiankang of Emperor Cheng of Jin, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin there was drought.

sentences.zh: 是時成帝沖弱，不親萬機，內外之政，委之將相。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Cheng was young and weak, not personally handling the myriad affairs of state; internal and external government was entrusted to generals and chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Cheng was still a child and did not personally handle affairs of state; both internal and external government was entrusted to generals and chancellors.

sentences.zh: 此僭踰之罰，故連歲旱也。

translations.literal: This was a penalty for presumption and overstepping—therefore drought year after year.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for presumption, and so there was drought year after year.

sentences.zh: 至四年，王導固讓太傅，復子明辟，是後不旱，殆其應也。

translations.literal: By the fourth year, Wang Dao firmly declined the title of Grand Tutor and restored the Son of Heaven to clear governance; after this there was no drought—perhaps the corresponding response.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth year Wang Dao steadfastly declined the Grand Tutorship and restored the Son to bright governance; drought ceased thereafter—perhaps the fulfillment of that change.

sentences.zh: 時天下普旱，會稽餘姚特甚，米斗直五百，民有相鬻。

translations.literal: At the time drought was universal under Heaven; Kuaiji and Yuyao were especially severe—a dou of rice cost five hundred cash; among the people some sold each other.
translations.idiomatic: At the time drought afflicted the realm; Kuaiji and Yuyao suffered especially severely—a dou of rice sold for five hundred cash, and some among the people sold one another.

sentences.zh: 咸康二年三月，旱。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Xiankang, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Xiankang there was drought.

sentences.zh: 咸康三年六月，旱。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Xiankang, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Xiankang there was drought.

sentences.zh: 晉康帝建元元年五月，旱。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Jianyuan of Emperor Kang of Jin, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Jianyuan under Emperor Kang of Jin there was drought.

sentences.zh: 是時宰相專政，方伯擅重兵，又與咸康初同事也。

translations.literal: At this time the chancellor monopolized government; regional lords wielded heavy armies alone—again the same matter as the beginning of Xiankang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the chancellor monopolized government and regional lords wielded heavy armies at will—the same case as at the beginning of Xiankang.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝永和元年五月，旱。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yonghe of Emperor Mu of Jin, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu of Jin there was drought.

sentences.zh: 有司奏依董仲舒術，徙市開水門，遣謁者祭太社。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized following the methods of Dong Zhongshu: move the market and open the water gate; dispatch an internuncio to sacrifice at the Grand Altar of Soil.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials memorialized that, following Dong Zhongshu's methods, the market should be moved, the water gate opened, and an internuncio dispatched to sacrifice at the Grand Altar of Soil.

sentences.zh: 是時帝在繈抱，褚太后臨朝如明穆太后故事。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor was still in swaddling clothes; Empress Dowager Chu presided at court following the precedent of Empress Dowager Mingmu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor was still an infant in swaddling clothes, and Empress Dowager Chu held court following the precedent of Empress Dowager Mingmu.

sentences.zh: 永和五年七月，不雨，至于十月。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghe, in the seventh month no rain until the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Yonghe no rain fell until the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 是年二月，征北將軍褚裒遣軍伐沛，納其民以歸。

translations.literal: That year in the second month, the General Who Conquers the North Chu Pou dispatched troops to attack Pei and brought its people back under submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of that year the General Who Conquers the North Chu Pou dispatched troops to attack Pei and brought its people back under submission.

sentences.zh: 六月，又遣西中郎將陳逵進據壽陽，自以舟師二萬至于下邳，喪其前驅而還，逵亦退。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, they again sent the Western Palace Gentleman-Commander Chen Kui to advance and hold Shouyang; Chu Pou himself led twenty thousand river troops as far as Xiapi, lost his vanguard and returned; Kui also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the court again sent the Western Palace Gentleman-Commander Chen Kui to advance and hold Shouyang; Chu Pou himself led twenty thousand river troops as far as Xiapi, lost his vanguard, and withdrew, and Kui also retreated.

sentences.zh: 永和六年閏月，旱。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month of the sixth year of Yonghe, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month of the sixth year of Yonghe there was drought.

sentences.zh: 是春，桓溫以大眾出夏口，上疏欲以舟軍北伐，朝廷駭之。

translations.literal: That spring, Huan Wen marched out of Xiakou with a great host; he submitted a memorial wishing to conduct a northern campaign by river forces—the court was alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Huan Wen marched out of Xiakou with a great host and submitted a memorial proposing a northern campaign by river forces, alarming the court.

sentences.zh: 蕭敬文盜涪，西蠻校尉采壽敗績。

translations.literal: Xiao Jingwen pillaged Fu; the Commandant of the Western Barbarians Cai Shou suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jingwen pillaged Fu, and the Commandant of the Western Barbarians, Cai Shou, suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝升平三年十二月，大旱。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Shengping of Emperor Mu of Jin, great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of Shengping under Emperor Mu of Jin there was a great drought.

sentences.zh: 此冬十月，北中郎將郄曇帥萬餘人出高平，經略河、兗；

translations.literal: This winter in the tenth month, the Northern Palace Gentleman-Commander Xi Tan led more than ten thousand men out of Gaoping to secure the He and Yan regions;
translations.idiomatic: This winter, in the tenth month, the Northern Palace Gentleman-Commander Xi Tan led more than ten thousand men out of Gaoping to secure the He and Yan regions;

sentences.zh: 又遣將軍諸葛悠以舟軍入河，敗績。

translations.literal: They also sent the General Zhuge You with river forces into the Yellow River and suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The court also sent the General Zhuge You with river forces into the Yellow River and suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 西中郎將謝萬次下蔡，眾潰而歸。

translations.literal: The Western Palace Gentleman-Commander Xie Wan encamped at Xiacai; the troops routed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Palace Gentleman-Commander Xie Wan encamped at Xiacai, but his troops routed and returned.

sentences.zh: 升平四年十二月，大旱。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Shengping, great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Shengping there was a great drought.

sentences.zh: 晉哀帝隆和元年夏，旱。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Longhe of Emperor Ai of Jin, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the first year of Longhe under Emperor Ai of Jin there was drought.

sentences.zh: 是時桓溫強恣，權制朝廷，僭踰之罰也。

translations.literal: At this time Huan Wen was powerful and willful, controlling the court by force—the penalty for presumption and overstepping.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huan Wen was powerful and willful and controlled the court by force—the penalty for presumption.

sentences.zh: 又去年慕容恪圍冀州刺史呂護，桓溫出次宛陵，范汪、袁真並北伐，眾出過時也。

translations.literal: Moreover last year Murong Ke besieged the Inspector of Ji Province Lu Hu; Huan Wen went out and encamped at Wanling; Fan Wang and Yuan Zhen both conducted northern campaigns—troops went out beyond the proper season.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the previous year Murong Ke besieged the Inspector of Ji Province, Lu Hu; Huan Wen marched out and encamped at Wanling; Fan Wang and Yuan Zhen both launched northern campaigns—troops had been deployed beyond the proper season.

sentences.zh: 晉海西太和四年十二月，涼州春旱至夏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Taihe of the Deposed Emperor of Jin, in Liang Province spring drought lasted until summer.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Taihe under the Deposed Emperor of Jin, Liang Province suffered drought from spring until summer.

sentences.zh: 晉簡文帝咸安二年十月，大旱民飢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Xian'an of Emperor Jianwen of Jin, great drought and the people starved.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Xian'an under Emperor Jianwen of Jin there was great drought and the people faced famine.

sentences.zh: 是時嗣主幼沖，桓溫陵僭。

translations.literal: At this time the successor lord was young and tender; Huan Wen was overbearing and presumptuous.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the successor sovereign was still a child, and Huan Wen was overbearing and presumptuous.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝寧康元年二月，旱。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Ningkang of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Ningkang under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin there was drought.

sentences.zh: 是時桓溫入覲高平陵，闔朝致拜，踰僭之應也。

translations.literal: At this time Huan Wen entered court to attend at the Gaoping Mausoleum; the whole court paid obeisance—the fulfillment of exceeding presumption.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huan Wen entered court to attend at the Gaoping Mausoleum, and the whole court paid obeisance—the fulfillment of excess and presumption.

sentences.zh: 寧康三年冬，旱。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Ningkang, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Ningkang there was drought.

sentences.zh: 先是，氐賊破梁、益州，刺史揚亮、周仲孫奔退。

translations.literal: Before this, the Di rebels broke Liang and Yizhou; the Inspectors Yang Liang and Zhou Zhongsun fled and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Di rebels had overrun Liang and Yizhou, and the Inspectors Yang Liang and Zhou Zhongsun fled.

sentences.zh: 明年，威遠將軍桓石虔擊姚萇墊江，破之，退至五城。

translations.literal: The next year, the General Who Establishes Distant Might Huan Shiqian struck Yao Chang at Dianjiang, defeated him, and withdrew to Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the General Who Establishes Distant Might Huan Shiqian attacked Yao Chang at Dianjiang, defeated him, and withdrew to Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史竺瑤帥眾戍巴東。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yizhou Zhu Yao led troops to garrison Badong.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector of Yizhou Zhu Yao led troops to garrison Badong.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元四年六月，大旱。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin there was a great drought.

sentences.zh: 去歲，氐賊圍南中郎將朱序於襄陽，又圍揚威將軍戴遁於彭城。

translations.literal: Last year the Di rebels besieged the Southern Palace Gentleman-Commander Zhu Xu at Xiangyang and also besieged the General Who Displays Might Dai Dun at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous year the Di rebels besieged the Southern Palace Gentleman-Commander Zhu Xu at Xiangyang and also besieged the General Who Displays Might Dai Dun at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 桓嗣以江州之眾次鄀援序，北府發三州民配何謙救遁。

translations.literal: Huan Si with the troops of Jiang Province encamped at E to relieve Xu; the Northern Headquarters mobilized the people of three provinces and assigned them to He Qian to rescue Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Si led the troops of Jiang Province to encamp at E and relieve Xu, while the Northern Headquarters mobilized levies from three provinces and assigned them to He Qian to rescue Dun.

sentences.zh: 是春，襄陽、順陽、魏興城皆沒。

translations.literal: That spring, the cities of Xiangyang, Shunyang, and Weixing all fell.
translations.idiomatic: That spring the cities of Xiangyang, Shunyang, and Weixing all fell.

sentences.zh: 賊遂略淮南，向廣陵。

translations.literal: The rebels then overran Huainan and advanced toward Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then overran Huainan and advanced toward Guangling.

sentences.zh: 征虜將軍謝石率水軍次涂中。

translations.literal: The General Who Conquers the Barbarians Xie Shi led river forces to encamp at Tuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The General Who Conquers the Barbarians Xie Shi led river forces to encamp at Tuzhong.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史謝玄督諸將破之。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yan Province Xie Xuan supervised the generals and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector of Yan Province Xie Xuan directed the generals and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 太元八年六月，旱。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighth year of Taiyuan, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eighth year of Taiyuan there was drought.

sentences.zh: 夏初，桓沖征襄陽，遣冠軍將軍桓石虔進據樊城。

translations.literal: At the beginning of summer, Huan Chong campaigned against Xiangyang and sent the Champion General Huan Shiqian to advance and hold Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of summer Huan Chong campaigned against Xiangyang and sent the Champion General Huan Shiqian to advance and hold Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又遣宣城內史胡彬次峽石為沖聲勢也。

translations.literal: The court also sent the Administrator of Xuancheng Hu Bin to encamp at Xiashi to bolster Chong's display of force.
translations.idiomatic: The court also sent the Administrator of Xuancheng Hu Bin to encamp at Xiashi to support Chong's display of force.

sentences.zh: 太元十年七月，旱饑。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year of Taiyuan, drought and famine.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the tenth year of Taiyuan there was drought and famine.

sentences.zh: 初八年，破苻堅；

translations.literal: In the beginning, in the eighth year they defeated Fu Jian;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the eighth year they had defeated Fu Jian;

sentences.zh: 九年，諸將略地，有事徐、豫；

translations.literal: in the ninth year, the generals overran territory and had military affairs in Xu and Yu;
translations.idiomatic: in the ninth year the generals had overrun territory and were active in Xu and Yu;

sentences.zh: 楊亮、趙統攻討巴、沔。

translations.literal: Yang Liang and Zhao Tong attacked and suppressed Ba and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Liang and Zhao Tong attacked and suppressed Ba and Mian.

sentences.zh: 是年正月，謝安又出鎮廣陵，使子琰進次彭城。

translations.literal: That year in the first month, Xie An again went out to govern at Guangling and had his son Yan advance to encamp at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of that year Xie An again went out to govern at Guangling and had his son Yan advance to encamp at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 太元十三年六月，旱。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year of Taiyuan, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year of Taiyuan there was drought.

sentences.zh: 去歲，北府遣戍胡陸，荊州經略河南。

translations.literal: Last year the Northern Headquarters dispatched garrisons to Hulu; Jing Province secured Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous year the Northern Headquarters had garrisoned Hulu, and Jing Province had secured Henan.

sentences.zh: 是年，郭銓置戍野王，又遣軍破黃淮。

translations.literal: That year, Guo Qian established a garrison at Yewang and also dispatched troops to break the Huang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: That year Guo Qian established a garrison at Yewang and also dispatched troops to break through the Huang and Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 太元十五年七月，旱。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifteenth year of Taiyuan, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifteenth year of Taiyuan there was drought.

sentences.zh: 是春，丁零略兗、豫，鮮卑寇河上。

translations.literal: That spring, the Dingling overran Yan and Yu; the Xianbei raided the banks of the river.
translations.idiomatic: That spring the Dingling overran Yan and Yu, and the Xianbei raided the northern river banks.

sentences.zh: 朱序、桓不才等北至太行，東至滑臺，踰時攻討，又戍石門。

translations.literal: Zhu Xu, Huan Bucai, and others reached the Taihang Mountains in the north and Huatai in the east; campaigns extended beyond the proper season, and they also garrisoned Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu, Huan Bucai, and others reached as far north as the Taihang Mountains and as far east as Huatai; campaigns extended beyond the proper season, and they also garrisoned Shimen.

sentences.zh: 太元十七年秋，旱，至冬。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventeenth year of Taiyuan, drought lasting until winter.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventeenth year of Taiyuan drought persisted until winter.

sentences.zh: 是時茹千秋為驃騎諮議，竊弄主相威福；

translations.literal: At this time Ru Qianqiu served as Military Adviser to the Rapid Cavalry General and secretly wielded the authority and benefits of lord and chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ru Qianqiu served as Military Adviser to the Rapid Cavalry General and secretly wielded the authority and favors of lord and chancellor;

sentences.zh: 又丘尼乳母親黨及婢僕之子，階緣近習，臨民領眾。

translations.literal: moreover the milk kin of nuns and the relatives of wet nurses, together with sons of maidservants and bondsmen, climbed up through close attendance and governed the people and commanded troops.
translations.idiomatic: moreover the milk kin of nuns, the relatives of wet nurses, and even sons of maidservants and bondsmen rose through proximity to power and governed the people and commanded troops.

sentences.zh: 又在所多上春竟囚，不以其辜，建康獄吏枉暴尤甚。

translations.literal: Moreover in their jurisdictions they often petitioned for spring amnesty for completed prisoners without regard to guilt; the prison officers of Jiankang were especially arbitrary and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover in their jurisdictions they often secured spring amnesty for prisoners whose cases had concluded, without regard to guilt, and the prison officers of Jiankang were especially arbitrary and cruel.

sentences.zh: 此僭踰不從，寃濫之罰也。

translations.literal: This was presumption, overstepping, and not heeding words—the penalty for wrongful imprisonment and abuse.
translations.idiomatic: This was presumption, disobedience, and the penalty for wrongful imprisonment and abuse.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安四年五月，旱。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Long'an of Emperor An of Jin, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Long'an under Emperor An of Jin there was drought.

sentences.zh: 去冬桓玄迫殺殷仲堪，而朝廷即授以荊州之任；

translations.literal: Last winter Huan Xuan forced and killed Yin Zhongkan, yet the court immediately granted him the post in Jing Province;
translations.idiomatic: The previous winter Huan Xuan had forced and killed Yin Zhongkan, yet the court immediately granted him the post in Jing Province;

sentences.zh: 司馬元顯又諷百僚悉使敬己。

translations.literal: Sima Yuanxian also prompted the hundred officials to make all revere himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yuanxian also pressured the hundred officials to show him reverence.

sentences.zh: 此皆陵僭之罰也。

translations.literal: These were all penalties for overbearing presumption.
translations.idiomatic: These were all penalties for overbearing presumption.

sentences.zh: 隆安五年夏秋，大旱，十二月不雨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Long'an, summer and autumn had great drought; in the twelfth month there was no rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Long'an there was great drought in summer and autumn, and in the twelfth month still no rain fell.

sentences.zh: 去年夏，孫恩入會稽，殺內史謝琰；

translations.literal: Last summer Sun En entered Kuaiji and killed the Interior Minister Xie Yan;
translations.idiomatic: The previous summer Sun En had entered Kuaiji and killed the Interior Minister Xie Yan;

sentences.zh: 此年夏，略吳，又殺內史袁山松。

translations.literal: This summer he overran Wu and also killed the Interior Minister Yuan Shansong.
translations.idiomatic: This summer he overran Wu and also killed the Interior Minister Yuan Shansong.

sentences.zh: 軍旅東討，眾出過時。

translations.literal: Armies marched east in punitive campaigns—troops went out beyond the proper season.
translations.idiomatic: Armies marched east on punitive campaigns, and troops were deployed beyond the proper season.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝元興元年七月，大饑，九月十月不雨。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Yuanxing of Emperor An of Jin, great famine; in the ninth and tenth months no rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Yuanxing under Emperor An of Jin there was great famine, and in the ninth and tenth months no rain fell.

sentences.zh: 是年正月，司馬元顯以大眾將討桓玄，既而玄至，殺元顯。

translations.literal: That year in the first month, Sima Yuanxian with a great host was about to campaign against Huan Xuan; soon afterward Xuan arrived and killed Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of that year Sima Yuanxian prepared to campaign against Huan Xuan with a great host, but Huan Xuan soon arrived and killed Yuanxian.

sentences.zh: 五月，又遣東征孫恩餘黨，十月，北討劉軌。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, they again dispatched an eastern campaign against the remnant faction of Sun En; in the tenth month, a northern campaign against Liu Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the court again dispatched an eastern campaign against Sun En's remnant faction, and in the tenth month a northern campaign against Liu Gui.

sentences.zh: 元興二年六月，不雨，冬，又旱。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanxing, in the sixth month no rain; in winter, drought again.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Yuanxing no rain fell, and in winter there was drought again.

sentences.zh: 是時桓玄奢僭，十二月，遂篡位。

translations.literal: At this time Huan Xuan was lavish and presumptuous; in the twelfth month he usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huan Xuan was lavish and presumptuous, and in the twelfth month he usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 元興三年八月，不雨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Yuanxing, no rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Yuanxing no rain fell.

sentences.zh: 是時王旅四伐，西夏未平。

translations.literal: At this time the royal armies campaigned on four fronts; the Western Xia was not yet pacified.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the royal armies campaigned on four fronts, and the western regions were not yet pacified.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙六年九月，不雨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year of Yixi of Emperor An of Jin, no rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin no rain fell.

sentences.zh: 是時王師北討廣固，疆理三州。

translations.literal: At this time the royal army campaigned north against Guanggu and defined the boundaries of three provinces.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the royal army campaigned north against Guanggu and reorganized the boundaries of three provinces.

sentences.zh: 義熙八年十月，不雨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year of Yixi, no rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eighth year of Yixi no rain fell.

sentences.zh: 是秋，王師西討劉毅；

translations.literal: That autumn, the royal army campaigned west against Liu Yi;
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the royal army campaigned west against Liu Yi;

sentences.zh: 分遣伐蜀。

translations.literal: detachments were also dispatched to attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: detachments were also dispatched to attack Shu.

sentences.zh: 義熙十年九月，旱，十二月，又旱。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the tenth year of Yixi, drought; in the twelfth month, drought again.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the tenth year of Yixi there was drought, and in the twelfth month drought again.

sentences.zh: 井瀆多竭。

translations.literal: Wells and drainage channels mostly dried up.
translations.idiomatic: Wells and drainage channels for the most part ran dry.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二年夏，旱。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song there was drought.

sentences.zh: 元嘉四年秋，京都旱。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year of Yuanjia, the capital had drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year of Yuanjia the capital suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 元嘉八年五月，揚州諸郡旱。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Yuanjia, the various commanderies of Yang Province had drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Yuanjia drought afflicted the various commanderies of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十九年、二十年，南兗、豫州旱。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth and twentieth years of Yuanjia, South Yan and Yu Provinces had drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth and twentieth years of Yuanjia South Yan and Yu Provinces suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年八月，不雨，至二十八年三月。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, no rain until the third month of the twenty-eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia no rain fell until the third month of the twenty-eighth year.

sentences.zh: 時索虜南寇。

translations.literal: At the time the northern barbarians raided south.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the northern barbarians were raiding south.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明七年、八年，東諸郡大旱，民飢死者十六七。

translations.literal: In the seventh and eighth years of Daming of Emperor Xiaowu, the eastern commanderies had great drought; among the starving people six or seven in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh and eighth years of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu the eastern commanderies suffered great drought, and six or seven in ten among the starving people died.

sentences.zh: 先是江左以來，制度多闕，孝武帝立明堂，造五輅。

translations.literal: Before this, since the establishment of the Jiang left, many institutions had been lacking; Emperor Xiaowu erected the Bright Hall and constructed the five chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, since the establishment of the realm south of the Yangzi, many institutions had been lacking; Emperor Xiaowu erected the Bright Hall and constructed the five ritual chariots.

sentences.zh: 是時大發徒眾，南巡校獵，盛自矜大，故致旱災。

translations.literal: At this time he massively mobilized conscript labor, conducted southern tours and hunting drives, and gloried in his own grandeur—therefore drought disaster came.
translations.idiomatic: At that time he massively mobilized conscript labor, toured the south on hunting expeditions, and gloried in his own grandeur, and so drought followed.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽元年八月，京都旱。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yuanhui of the Later Deposed Emperor, the capital had drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Yuanhui under the Later Deposed Emperor the capital suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 詩妖

translations.literal: Poetic prodigies
translations.idiomatic: Poetic Prodigies

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和中，京師歌兜鈴曹子，其唱曰：「其奈汝曹何。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era of Emperor Ming of Wei, the capital sang the Dou-bell Cao-zi; its refrain said: "What can be done about you Cao fellows?"
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era of Emperor Ming of Wei the capital sang the Dou-bell Cao-zi, whose refrain ran: "What can be done about you Cao fellows?"

sentences.zh: 此詩妖也。

translations.literal: This was a poetic prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: This was a poetic prodigy.

sentences.zh: 其後曹爽見誅，曹氏遂廢。

translations.literal: Afterward Cao Shuang was executed, and the house of Cao was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Cao Shuang was executed and the house of Cao was abolished.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝景初中，童謠曰：「阿公阿公駕馬車，不意阿公東渡河。

translations.literal: In the Jingchu era of Emperor Ming of Wei, a children's rhyme said: "Grandfather, grandfather, driving a horse carriage—who thought grandfather would cross the river east?"
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingchu era of Emperor Ming of Wei a children's rhyme ran: "Grandfather, grandfather, driving a horse carriage—who thought grandfather would cross the river east?"

sentences.zh: 阿公東還當奈何！

translations.literal: When grandfather returns east, what then shall be done!
translations.idiomatic: When grandfather returns east, what then shall be done!

sentences.zh: 」及宣王平遼東，歸至白屋，當還鎮長安。

translations.literal: When the Lord of Xuan pacified Liaodong and returned to Baiwu, he was about to go back to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lord of Xuan pacified Liaodong and returned to Baiwu, he was about to go back and garrison Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 會帝疾篤，急召之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Emperor's illness was grave, and he urgently summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the Emperor's illness was grave, and he urgently summoned him.

sentences.zh: 乃乘追鋒車東渡河，終翦魏室，如童謠之言也。

translations.literal: He then rode a pursuit chariot east across the river and in the end cut down the house of Wei, just as the children's rhyme had said.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode a pursuit chariot east across the river and in the end cut down the house of Wei, just as the children's rhyme had said.

sentences.zh: 魏齊王嘉平中，有謠曰：「白馬素覊西南馳，其誰乘者朱虎騎。

translations.literal: In the Jiaping era of Emperor Qi of Wei, there was a rhyme that said: "A white horse with plain reins gallops southwest—who rides it but Zhu the Tiger Knight?"
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiaping era of Emperor Qi of Wei a rhyme ran: "A white horse with plain reins gallops southwest—who rides it but Zhu the Tiger Knight?"

sentences.zh: 」朱虎者，楚王彪小字也。

translations.literal: Zhu the Tiger was the childhood name of Prince of Chu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu the Tiger was the childhood name of Prince of Chu Biao.

sentences.zh: 王淩、令狐愚聞此謠，謀立彪。

translations.literal: Wang Ling and Linghu Yu heard this rhyme and plotted to install Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling and Linghu Yu heard this rhyme and plotted to install Biao.

sentences.zh: 事發，淩等伏誅，彪賜死。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, Ling and the others were executed, and Biao was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was exposed, Ling and the others were executed, and Biao was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮初，童謠曰：「吁汝恪，何若若，蘆葦單衣篾鈎絡，於何相求成子閣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sun Liang's reign in Wu, a children's rhyme said: "Ah, you Ke, how grand you are—reed matting for a single garment, bamboo strips for a belt hook; where do you seek the Pavilion of the Son Cheng?"
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Sun Liang's reign in Wu a children's rhyme ran: "Ah, you Ke, how grand you are—reed matting for a single garment, bamboo strips for a belt hook; where do you seek the Pavilion of the Son Cheng?"

sentences.zh: 」成子閣者，反語石子堈也。

translations.literal: The Pavilion of the Son Cheng, read in reverse, is the Stone Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The Pavilion of the Son Cheng, read in reverse, is the Stone Mound.

sentences.zh: 鈎落，釣帶也。

translations.literal: A hook falling is a fishing belt.
translations.idiomatic: A hook falling refers to a fishing belt.

sentences.zh: 及諸葛恪死，果以葦席裹身，篾束其要，投之石子堈。

translations.literal: When Zhuge Ke died, he was indeed wrapped in a reed mat, his waist bound with bamboo strips, and cast into the Stone Mound.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Ke died, he was indeed wrapped in a reed mat, his waist bound with bamboo strips, and cast into the Stone Mound.

sentences.zh: 後聽恪故吏收歛，求之此堈云。

translations.literal: Later, when Ke's former clerks were permitted to gather his remains, they searched for him at this mound, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Ke's former clerks were permitted to gather his remains, they searched for him at this mound, it is said.

sentences.zh: 孫亮初，公安有白鼉鳴。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sun Liang's reign, at Gong'an a white alligator cried out.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Sun Liang's reign a white alligator cried out at Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 童謠曰：「白鼉鳴，龜背平，南郡城中可長生，守死不去義無成。

translations.literal: A children's rhyme said: "The white alligator cries, the turtle's back is flat; within the city of Nan Commandery one may live long—hold fast and die without fleeing, for righteousness cannot succeed."
translations.idiomatic: A children's rhyme ran: "The white alligator cries, the turtle's back is flat; within the city of Nan Commandery one may live long—hold fast and die without fleeing, for righteousness cannot succeed."

sentences.zh: 」南郡城可長生者，有急，易以逃也。

translations.literal: The city of Nan Commandery where one may live long means that in an emergency one may easily escape.
translations.idiomatic: The city of Nan Commandery where one may live long means that in an emergency one may easily escape.

sentences.zh: 明年，諸葛恪敗，弟融鎮公安，亦見襲。

translations.literal: The next year Zhuge Ke was defeated; his younger brother Rong, garrisoning Gong'an, was also attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhuge Ke was defeated, and his younger brother Rong, garrisoning Gong'an, was also attacked.

sentences.zh: 融刮金印龜，服之而死。

translations.literal: Rong scraped the gold from the seal turtle and swallowed it to die.
translations.idiomatic: Rong scraped the gold from the seal turtle and swallowed it to die.

sentences.zh: 鼉有鱗介，甲兵之象。

translations.literal: The alligator has scales and armor—the image of armored troops.
translations.idiomatic: The alligator has scales and armor—the image of armored troops.

sentences.zh: 又白兵祥也。

translations.literal: Moreover white is an omen of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover white is an omen of warfare.

sentences.zh: 孫休永安二年，將守質子羣聚嬉戲，有異小子忽來，言曰：「三公鋤，司馬如。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an of Sun Xiu, hostage sons of generals and garrison commanders gathered to play; a strange youth suddenly came and said: "The Three Dukes are hoed under; the Sima is like."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yong'an of Sun Xiu the hostage sons of generals and garrison commanders gathered to play; a strange youth suddenly appeared and said: "The Three Dukes are hoed under; the Sima is like."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「我非人，熒惑星也。

translations.literal: He also said: "I am not human—I am the Sparkling Deluder star."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "I am not human—I am the Sparkling Deluder star."

sentences.zh: 」言畢上升，仰視若曳一匹練，有頃沒。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he ascended; looking up, it was as if a bolt of silk were trailing; in a moment he vanished.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished speaking he ascended; looking up, it was as if a bolt of silk were trailing; in a moment he vanished.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰，後四年而蜀亡，六年而魏廢，二十一年而吳平，於是九服歸晉。

translations.literal: Gan Bao says: four years later Shu perished; six years later Wei was abolished; twenty-one years later Wu was pacified; then the nine domains returned to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao says that four years later Shu perished, six years later Wei was abolished, twenty-one years later Wu was pacified, and then the nine domains returned to Jin.

sentences.zh: 魏與吳、蜀，並為戰國，「三公鋤，司馬如」之謂也。

translations.literal: Wei together with Wu and Shu were all warring states—this is what is meant by "The Three Dukes are hoed under; the Sima is like."
translations.idiomatic: Wei together with Wu and Shu were all warring states—this is what is meant by "The Three Dukes are hoed under; the Sima is like."

sentences.zh: 孫晧初，童謠曰：「寧飲建業水，不食武昌魚；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sun Hao's reign, a children's rhyme said: "Better drink the water of Jianye than eat the fish of Wuchang;"
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Sun Hao's reign a children's rhyme ran: "Better drink the water of Jianye than eat the fish of Wuchang;"

sentences.zh: 寧還建業死，不止武昌居。

translations.literal: "Better return to Jianye to die than remain dwelling at Wuchang."
translations.idiomatic: "Better return to Jianye to die than remain dwelling at Wuchang."

sentences.zh: 」晧尋遷都武昌，民泝流供給，咸怨毒焉。

translations.literal: Hao soon moved the capital to Wuchang; the people went upstream to supply provisions, and all resented it bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Hao soon moved the capital to Wuchang; the people had to go upstream to supply provisions, and all resented it bitterly.

sentences.zh: 孫晧遣使者祭石印山下妖祠。

translations.literal: Sun Hao dispatched an envoy to sacrifice at the demonic shrine beneath Mount Shiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao dispatched an envoy to sacrifice at the demonic shrine beneath Mount Shiyin.

sentences.zh: 使者因以丹書巖曰：「楚九州渚，吳九州都。

translations.literal: The envoy then wrote in cinnabar on the cliff: "Chu had the islets of the nine domains; Wu has the capital of the nine domains."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy then wrote in cinnabar on the cliff: "Chu had the islets of the nine domains; Wu has the capital of the nine domains."

sentences.zh: 揚州士，作天子。

translations.literal: "The gentry of Yang Province shall become Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: "The gentry of Yang Province shall become Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 四世治，太平矣。

translations.literal: "Four generations in good order—great peace has come."
translations.idiomatic: "Four generations in good order—great peace has come."

sentences.zh: 」晧聞之，意益張，曰：「從大皇帝至朕四世，太平之主，非朕復誰？

translations.literal: When Hao heard this, his mind grew still more inflated, and he said: "From the Grand Emperor down to myself for four generations—lords of great peace—if not myself, then who?"
translations.idiomatic: When Hao heard this, his mind grew still more inflated, and he said: "From the Grand Emperor down to myself for four generations—lords of great peace—if not myself, then who?"

sentences.zh: 」恣虐踰甚，尋以降亡。

translations.literal: He indulged in cruelty beyond measure and soon submitted and perished.
translations.idiomatic: He indulged in cruelty beyond measure and soon submitted and perished.

sentences.zh: 近詩妖也。

translations.literal: This was a recent poetic prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: This was a recent poetic prodigy.

sentences.zh: 孫晧天紀中，童謠曰：「阿童復阿童，銜刀游渡江。

translations.literal: In the Tianji era of Sun Hao, a children's rhyme said: "Ah Tong again, Ah Tong, holding a blade roaming to cross the river."
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianji era of Sun Hao a children's rhyme ran: "Ah Tong again, Ah Tong, holding a blade roaming to cross the river."

sentences.zh: 不畏岸上虎，但畏水中龍。

translations.literal: "Not fearing the tiger on the bank, but fearing only the dragon in the water."
translations.idiomatic: "Not fearing the tiger on the bank, but fearing only the dragon in the water."

sentences.zh: 」晉武帝聞之，加王濬龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Jin heard this, he promoted Wang Jun to General of the Soaring Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Jin heard this, he promoted Wang Jun to General of the Soaring Dragon.

sentences.zh: 及征吳，江西眾軍無過者，而王濬先定秣陵。

translations.literal: When they campaigned against Wu, none of the armies west of the river surpassed him, and Wang Jun was first to secure Moling.
translations.idiomatic: When they campaigned against Wu, none of the armies west of the river surpassed him, and Wang Jun was first to secure Moling.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康後，江南童謠曰：「局縮肉，數橫目，中國當敗吳當復。

translations.literal: After Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, a children's rhyme in Jiangnan said: "Shrunken flesh, counting horizontal eyes—China shall fall and Wu shall rise again."
translations.idiomatic: After Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin a children's rhyme in Jiangnan ran: "Shrunken flesh, counting horizontal eyes—China shall fall and Wu shall rise again."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「宮門柱，且莫朽，吳當復，在三十年後。

translations.literal: It also said: "The palace gate pillars—do not yet decay; Wu shall rise again, thirty years hence."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "The palace gate pillars—do not yet decay; Wu shall rise again, thirty years hence."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「雞鳴不拊翼，吳復不用力。

translations.literal: It also said: "The cock crows without beating its wings—Wu rises again without effort."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "The cock crows without beating its wings—Wu rises again without effort."

sentences.zh: 」于時吳人皆謂在孫氏子孫，故竊發亂者相繼。

translations.literal: At the time the people of Wu all believed it referred to Sun clan descendants, and so secret uprisings followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the people of Wu all believed it referred to Sun clan descendants, and so secret uprisings followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 按橫目者「四」字，自吳亡至晉元帝興，幾四十年，皆如童謠之言。

translations.literal: Examining it, horizontal eyes means the character "four"; from Wu's fall to the rise of Emperor Yuan of Jin was nearly forty years—all as the children's rhyme had said.
translations.idiomatic: Examining it, horizontal eyes means the character "four"; from Wu's fall to the rise of Emperor Yuan of Jin was nearly forty years—all as the children's rhyme had said.

sentences.zh: 元帝懦而少斷，局縮肉，直斥之也。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan was timid and lacking in resolve—"shrunken flesh" directly rebukes him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was timid and lacking in resolve—"shrunken flesh" directly rebukes him.

sentences.zh: 干寶云「不知所斥」，諱之也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao says "not knowing whom it rebukes"—this is euphemism.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao says "not knowing whom it rebukes"—this is euphemism.

sentences.zh: 太康末，京、洛始為「折楊柳」之歌，其曲始有兵革苦辛之詞，終以禽獲斬截之事。

translations.literal: At the end of Taikang, the capital and Luoyang first had the song "Breaking the Willow"; its tune at first had words of the hardship of arms and war, and ended with capture, beheading, and cutting down.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Taikang the capital and Luoyang first had the song "Breaking the Willow"; its tune at first had words of the hardship of arms and war, and ended with capture, beheading, and cutting down.

sentences.zh: 是時三楊貴盛而族滅，太后廢黜而幽死。

translations.literal: At this time the Three Yangs were noble and flourishing yet their clan was destroyed; the Empress Dowager was deposed and died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Three Yangs were noble and flourishing yet their clan was destroyed; the Empress Dowager was deposed and died in confinement.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永熙中，河內溫縣有人如狂，造書曰：「光光文長，大戟為牆。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era of Emperor Hui of Jin, in Wen County of Henei a man like one mad composed writing that said: "Bright bright Wen-chang, great halberds for a wall."
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era of Emperor Hui of Jin, in Wen County of Henei a man like one mad composed writing that said: "Bright bright Wen-chang, great halberds for a wall."

sentences.zh: 毒藥雖行，戟還自傷。

translations.literal: "Though poison is administered, the halberd still wounds itself."
translations.idiomatic: "Though poison is administered, the halberd still wounds itself."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「兩火沒地，哀哉秋蘭。

translations.literal: It also said: "Two fires sink into the earth—alas, autumn orchid."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "Two fires sink into the earth—alas, autumn orchid."

sentences.zh: 歸形街郵，路人為歎。

translations.literal: "Returning in form to Jieyou Street, passersby sigh for her."
translations.idiomatic: "Returning in form to Jieyou Street, passersby sigh for her."

sentences.zh: 」及楊駿居內府，以戟為衞，死時，又為戟所害。

translations.literal: When Yang Jun dwelt in the inner palace and used halberds for guard, at his death he was again harmed by halberds.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun dwelt in the inner palace and used halberds for guard, at his death he was again harmed by halberds.

sentences.zh: 楊太后被廢，賈后絕其膳，八日而崩，葬街郵亭北，百姓哀之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Yang was deposed; Empress Jia cut off her food, and after eight days she died; she was buried north of Jieyou Pavilion, and the common people mourned her.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Yang was deposed; Empress Jia cut off her food, and after eight days she died; she was buried north of Jieyou Pavilion, and the common people mourned her.

sentences.zh: 兩火，武帝諱；

translations.literal: Two fires is the taboo name of Emperor Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Two fires refers to the taboo name of Emperor Wu;

sentences.zh: 蘭，楊后字也。

translations.literal: Orchid is the style name of Empress Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Orchid is the style name of Empress Yang.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，童謠曰：「二月末，三月初，荊筆楊版行詔書，宮中大馬幾作驢。

translations.literal: In Yongxi, a children's rhyme said: "End of the second month, beginning of the third—Jing brush and Yang tablet issue the edict; the great horse in the palace nearly becomes a donkey."
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi a children's rhyme ran: "End of the second month, beginning of the third—Jing brush and Yang tablet issue the edict; the great horse in the palace nearly becomes a donkey."

sentences.zh: 」楊駿初專權，楚王尋用事，故言「荊筆楊版」也。

translations.literal: Yang Jun at first monopolized power; the Prince of Chu soon took charge of affairs—therefore it says "Jing brush and Yang tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun at first monopolized power; the Prince of Chu soon took charge of affairs—therefore it says "Jing brush and Yang tablet."

sentences.zh: 二人不誅，則君臣禮悖，故云「幾作驢」。

translations.literal: If the two men were not executed, then the rites between ruler and minister would be violated—therefore it says "nearly becomes a donkey."
translations.idiomatic: If the two men were not executed, then the rites between ruler and minister would be violated—therefore it says "nearly becomes a donkey."

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康中，京、洛童謠曰：「南風起，吹白沙，遙望魯國何嵯峨，千歲髑髏生齒牙。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of Jin, a children's rhyme in the capital and Luoyang said: "The south wind rises, blowing white sand; gazing afar at the State of Lu, how towering it is—a thousand-year skull grows teeth."
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of Jin a children's rhyme in the capital and Luoyang ran: "The south wind rises, blowing white sand; gazing afar at the State of Lu, how towering it is—a thousand-year skull grows teeth."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「城東馬子莫嚨哅，比至三月纏汝鬃。

translations.literal: It also said: "The horse colt east of the city, do not roar and bellow—by the third month it will wind your mane."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "The horse colt east of the city, do not roar and bellow—by the third month it will wind your mane."

sentences.zh: 」南風，賈后字也。

translations.literal: South wind is the style name of Empress Jia.
translations.idiomatic: South wind is the style name of Empress Jia.

sentences.zh: 白，晉行也。

translations.literal: White is the element of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: White is the element of Jin.

sentences.zh: 沙門，太子小名也。

translations.literal: Shamen is the childhood name of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Shamen is the childhood name of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 魯，賈謐國也。

translations.literal: Lu is the fief of Jia Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu is the fief of Jia Mi.

sentences.zh: 言賈后將與謐為亂，以危太子；

translations.literal: It means Empress Jia would join with Mi in rebellion to endanger the Crown Prince;
translations.idiomatic: It means Empress Jia would join with Mi in rebellion to endanger the Crown Prince;

sentences.zh: 而趙王因釁咀嚼豪賢，以成篡奪也。

translations.literal: and the Prince of Zhao would seize the occasion to chew up the great and worthy and accomplish usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: and the Prince of Zhao would seize the occasion to chew up the great and worthy and accomplish usurpation.

sentences.zh: 是時愍懷頗失眾望，卒以廢黜，不得其死。

translations.literal: At this time Minhuai had largely lost the people's hopes and in the end was deposed and did not meet a natural death.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Minhuai had largely lost the people's hopes and in the end was deposed and did not meet a natural death.

sentences.zh: 元康中，天下商農通著大鄣日，童謠曰：「屠蘇鄣日覆兩耳，當見瞎兒作天子。

translations.literal: In Yuankang, throughout the realm merchants and farmers commonly wore large sun-shields; a children's rhyme said: "Tusu shielding the sun covers both ears—you shall see a blind child become Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: In Yuankang, throughout the realm merchants and farmers commonly wore large sun-shields; a children's rhyme ran: "Tusu shielding the sun covers both ears—you shall see a blind child become Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」及趙王篡位，其目實眇焉。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Zhao usurped the throne, his eyes were indeed dim.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Zhao usurped the throne, his eyes were indeed dim.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫既篡，洛中童謠曰：「虎從北來鼻頭汗，龍從南來登城看，水從西來何灌灌。

translations.literal: After Prince of Zhao Lun had usurped, a children's rhyme in Luoyang said: "The tiger comes from the north with sweat on its nose; the dragon comes from the south to climb the wall and look; water comes from the west—how rushing it is."
translations.idiomatic: After Prince of Zhao Lun had usurped, a children's rhyme in Luoyang ran: "The tiger comes from the north with sweat on its nose; the dragon comes from the south to climb the wall and look; water comes from the west—how rushing it is."

sentences.zh: 」數月而齊王、成都、河間義兵同會誅倫。

translations.literal: Within several months the righteous armies of the Princes of Qi, Chengdu, and Hejian assembled together and executed Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Within several months the righteous armies of the Princes of Qi, Chengdu, and Hejian assembled together and executed Lun.

sentences.zh: 按成都西蕃而在鄴，故曰「虎從北來」；

translations.literal: Examining it, Chengdu was a western fief yet was at Ye—therefore it says "the tiger comes from the north";
translations.idiomatic: Examining it, Chengdu was a western fief yet was at Ye—therefore it says "the tiger comes from the north";

sentences.zh: 齊東蕃而在許，故曰「龍從南來」；

translations.literal: Qi was an eastern fief yet was at Xu—therefore it says "the dragon comes from the south";
translations.idiomatic: Qi was an eastern fief yet was at Xu—therefore it says "the dragon comes from the south";

sentences.zh: 河間水區而在關中，故曰「水從西來」。

translations.literal: Hejian was a water domain yet was in Guanzhong—therefore it says "water comes from the west."
translations.idiomatic: Hejian was a water domain yet was in Guanzhong—therefore it says "water comes from the west."

sentences.zh: 齊留輔政，居宮西，有無君之心，故言「登城看」也。

translations.literal: Qi remained to assist in government, dwelling west of the palace, with a mind lacking a ruler—therefore it says "climb the wall and look."
translations.idiomatic: Qi remained to assist in government, dwelling west of the palace, with a mind lacking a ruler—therefore it says "climb the wall and look."

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝太安中，童謠曰：「五馬游度江，一馬化為龍。

translations.literal: In the Tai'an era of Emperor Hui of Jin, a children's rhyme said: "Five horses roam crossing the river; one horse transforms into a dragon."
translations.idiomatic: In the Tai'an era of Emperor Hui of Jin a children's rhyme ran: "Five horses roam crossing the river; one horse transforms into a dragon."

sentences.zh: 」後中原大亂，宗蕃多絕，唯琅邪、汝南、西陽、南頓、彭城同至江表，而元帝嗣晉矣。

translations.literal: Afterward the Central Plains fell into great chaos; many of the imperial clans perished; only Langye, Runan, Xiyang, Nandun, and Pengcheng together reached the lands south of the river, and Emperor Yuan succeeded Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Central Plains fell into great chaos; many of the imperial clans perished; only Langye, Runan, Xiyang, Nandun, and Pengcheng together reached the lands south of the river, and Emperor Yuan succeeded Jin.

sentences.zh: 司馬越還洛，有童謠曰：「洛中大鼠長尺二，若不蚤去大狗至。

translations.literal: When Sima Yue returned to Luoyang, there was a children's rhyme that said: "The great rat in Luoyang is one chi and two cun long—if you do not leave early, the great dog will come."
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yue returned to Luoyang, a children's rhyme ran: "The great rat in Luoyang is one chi and two cun long—if you do not leave early, the great dog will come."

sentences.zh: 」及苟晞將破汲桑，又謠曰：「元超兄弟大落度，上桑打椹為苟作。

translations.literal: When Gou Xi was about to defeat Ji Sang, there was again a rhyme that said: "The Yuanchao brothers fall greatly; beating mulberries on the upper mulberry tree makes work for Gou."
translations.idiomatic: When Gou Xi was about to defeat Ji Sang, there was again a rhyme that ran: "The Yuanchao brothers fall greatly; beating mulberries on the upper mulberry tree makes work for Gou."

sentences.zh: 」由是越惡晞，奪其兗州，隙難遂構。

translations.literal: Because of this Yue hated Xi, stripped him of Yan Province, and enmity was thus formed.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this Yue hated Xi, stripped him of Yan Province, and enmity was thus formed.

sentences.zh: 晉愍帝建興中，江南歌謠曰：「訇如白阬破，合集持作甒。

translations.literal: In the Jianxing era of Emperor Min of Jin, a song in Jiangnan said: "With a crash like a white pit breaking, gather the pieces together and make a jar."
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianxing era of Emperor Min of Jin a song in Jiangnan ran: "With a crash like a white pit breaking, gather the pieces together and make a jar."

sentences.zh: 揚州破換敗，吳興覆瓿甊。

translations.literal: "Yang Province breaks and is ruined; Wuxing overturns its earthen jars."
translations.idiomatic: "Yang Province breaks and is ruined; Wuxing overturns its earthen jars."

sentences.zh: 」按白者晉行，阬器有口，屬甕，瓦質剛，亦金之類也。

translations.literal: Examining it, white is the element of Jin; a pit vessel has a mouth and belongs to the jar category; earthenware is hard in quality and is also of the metal kind.
translations.idiomatic: Examining it, white is the element of Jin; a pit vessel has a mouth and belongs to the jar category; earthenware is hard in quality and is also of the metal kind.

sentences.zh: 「訇如白阬破」者，言二都傾覆，王室大壞也。

translations.literal: "With a crash like a white pit breaking" means the two capitals toppled and the royal house was greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: "With a crash like a white pit breaking" means the two capitals toppled and the royal house was greatly ruined.

sentences.zh: 「合集持作甒」者，言元皇帝鳩集遺餘，以主社稷，未能克復中原，偏王江南，故其喻小也。

translations.literal: "Gather the pieces together and make a jar" means Emperor Yuan gathered the scattered remnants to uphold the altars of soil and grain, yet could not recover the Central Plains and ruled only partially in Jiangnan—therefore the metaphor is small.
translations.idiomatic: "Gather the pieces together and make a jar" means Emperor Yuan gathered the scattered remnants to uphold the altars of soil and grain, yet could not recover the Central Plains and ruled only partially in Jiangnan—therefore the metaphor is small.

sentences.zh: 及石頭之事，六軍大潰，兵人抄掠京邑，爰及二宮。

translations.literal: At the Shitou affair the six armies routed in great disorder; soldiers plundered the capital region, reaching even the two palaces.
translations.idiomatic: At the Shitou affair the six armies routed in great disorder; soldiers plundered the capital region, reaching even the two palaces.

sentences.zh: 其後三年，錢鳳復攻京邑，阻水而守，相持月餘日，焚燒城邑，井堙木刊矣。

translations.literal: Three years later Qian Feng again attacked the capital region, blocked by water and holding defense; they faced off for more than a month, burning cities and towns until wells were filled in and trees were cut down.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Qian Feng again attacked the capital region, blocked by water and holding defense; they faced off for more than a month, burning cities and towns until wells were filled in and trees were cut down.

sentences.zh: 鳳等敗退，沈充將其黨還吳興，官軍踵之，蹈藉郡縣。

translations.literal: Feng and the others were defeated and withdrew; Shen Chong led his faction back to Wuxing; the official armies followed and trampled the commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Feng and the others were defeated and withdrew; Shen Chong led his faction back to Wuxing; the official armies followed and trampled the commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 充父子授首，黨與誅者以百數。

translations.literal: Chong and his son surrendered their heads; associates executed numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and his son surrendered their heads; associates executed numbered in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 所謂「揚州破換敗，吳興覆瓿甊」。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by "Yang Province breaks and is ruined; Wuxing overturns its earthen jars."
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by "Yang Province breaks and is ruined; Wuxing overturns its earthen jars."

sentences.zh: 瓿甊，瓦器，又小於甒也。

translations.literal: Earthen jars are pottery vessels, again smaller than a jar.
translations.idiomatic: Earthen jars are pottery vessels, again smaller than a jar.

sentences.zh: 晉明帝太寧初，童謠歌曰：「惻力惻力，放馬山側。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taining of Emperor Ming of Jin, a children's rhyme song said: "Ce li, ce li, release the horses on the mountainside."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taining of Emperor Ming of Jin a children's rhyme song ran: "Ce li, ce li, release the horses on the mountainside."

sentences.zh: 大馬死，小馬餓，高山崩，石自破。

translations.literal: The great horse dies, the small horse starves; the high mountain collapses, the stone breaks of itself.
translations.idiomatic: The great horse dies, the small horse starves; the high mountain collapses, the stone breaks of itself.

sentences.zh: 」及明帝崩，成帝幼，為蘇峻所逼，遷于石頭，御饍不足。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Emperor Cheng was young and was pressed by Su Jun, moved to Shitou, and had insufficient imperial provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Emperor Cheng was still a child and was pressed by Su Jun, moved to Shitou, and had insufficient imperial provisions.

sentences.zh: 「高山崩」，言峻尋死；

translations.literal: "The high mountain collapses" means Jun would soon die;
translations.idiomatic: "The high mountain collapses" means Jun would soon die;

sentences.zh: 「石」，峻弟蘇石也，峻死後，石據石頭，尋為諸公所破也。

translations.literal: "Stone" is Jun's younger brother Su Shi; after Jun died, Shi held Shitou and was soon broken by the lords.
translations.idiomatic: "Stone" refers to Jun's younger brother Su Shi; after Jun died, Shi held Shitou and was soon defeated by the lords.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝之末，民間謠曰：「礚礚何隆隆，駕車入梓宮。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Cheng of Jin, a folk rhyme said: "Rumble, rumble—how thunderous! A carriage enters the imperial mausoleum."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Cheng of Jin a folk rhyme ran: "Rumble, rumble—how thunderous! A carriage enters the imperial mausoleum."

sentences.zh: 」少日而宮車晏駕。

translations.literal: Within a few days the imperial carriage departed at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days the imperial carriage departed at dusk.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康二年十二月，河北謠語曰：「麥入土，殺石虎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Xiankang of Emperor Cheng of Jin, a rhyme in Hebei said: "Wheat enters the earth—kill Shi Hu."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Xiankang of Emperor Cheng of Jin a rhyme in Hebei ran: "Wheat enters the earth—kill Shi Hu."

sentences.zh: 」後如謠言。

translations.literal: Afterward it happened as the rhyme had said.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward it happened as the rhyme had said.

sentences.zh: 庾亮初出鎮武昌，出石頭，百姓於岸上歌曰：「庾公上武昌，翩翩如飛鳥。

translations.literal: When Yu Liang first went out to govern Wuchang and left Shitou, the people on the bank sang: "Lord Yu goes up to Wuchang, light and graceful as a flying bird."
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Liang first went out to govern Wuchang and left Shitou, the people on the bank sang: "Lord Yu goes up to Wuchang, light and graceful as a flying bird."

sentences.zh: 庾公還揚州，白馬牽旒旐。

translations.literal: "Lord Yu returns to Yang Province—a white horse draws the funeral pennants."
translations.idiomatic: "Lord Yu returns to Yang Province—a white horse draws the funeral pennants."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「庾公初上時，翩翩如飛烏。

translations.literal: It also said: "When Lord Yu first went up, light and graceful as a flying crow."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "When Lord Yu first went up, light and graceful as a flying crow."

sentences.zh: 庾公還揚州，白馬牽流蘇。

translations.literal: "Lord Yu returns to Yang Province—a white horse draws the tassels."
translations.idiomatic: "Lord Yu returns to Yang Province—a white horse draws the tassels."

sentences.zh: 」後連徵不入，及薨，還都葬。

translations.literal: Later he was repeatedly summoned but did not enter; when he died, he was returned to the capital for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was repeatedly summoned but did not enter; when he died, he was returned to the capital for burial.

sentences.zh: 庾羲在吳郡，吳中童謠曰：「寧食下湖荇，不食上湖蓴。

translations.literal: When Yu Yi was in Wu Commandery, a children's rhyme in Wu said: "Better eat duckweed from the lower lake than eat water shield from the upper lake."
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yi was in Wu Commandery a children's rhyme in Wu ran: "Better eat duckweed from the lower lake than eat water shield from the upper lake."

sentences.zh: 庾吳沒命喪，復殺王領軍。

translations.literal: "Yu of Wu loses his life; again they kill the Commanding General Wang."
translations.idiomatic: "Yu of Wu loses his life; again they kill the Commanding General Wang."

sentences.zh: 」無幾而庾羲、王洽相繼亡。

translations.literal: Before long Yu Yi and Wang Qia died one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yu Yi and Wang Qia died one after another.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝升平中，童子輩忽歌於道曰「阿子聞」，曲終輒云「阿子汝聞不」。

translations.literal: In the Shengping era of Emperor Mu of Jin, groups of children suddenly sang in the streets "A-zi heard," and at the end of the tune always said "A-zi, did you hear?"
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengping era of Emperor Mu of Jin groups of children suddenly sang in the streets "A-zi heard," and at the end of the tune always said "A-zi, did you hear?"

sentences.zh: 無幾而穆帝崩，太后哭曰：「阿子汝聞不？」

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Mu died, and the Empress Dowager wept: "A-zi, did you hear?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Mu died, and the Empress Dowager wept: "A-zi, did you hear?"

sentences.zh: 升平末，民間忽作廉歌。

translations.literal: At the end of Shengping, the people suddenly made Lian songs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Shengping the people suddenly made Lian songs.

sentences.zh: 有扈謙者聞之，曰：「廉者臨也。

translations.literal: One Hu Qian heard it and said: "Lian means lin—approaching."
translations.idiomatic: One Hu Qian heard it and said: "Lian means lin—approaching."

sentences.zh: 歌云『白門廉，宮廷廉』，內外悉臨，國家其大諱乎？

translations.literal: The song says 'White Gate approaches, palace court approaches'—inside and outside all draw near; will the state meet its great taboo?"
translations.idiomatic: The song says 'White Gate approaches, palace court approaches'—inside and outside all draw near; will the state meet its great taboo?"

sentences.zh: 」少時而穆帝晏駕。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Mu departed at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Mu departed at dusk.

sentences.zh: 晉哀帝隆和初，童兒歌曰：「升平不滿斗，隆和那得久！

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longhe of Emperor Ai of Jin, children sang: "Shengping does not fill a dou—how can Longhe last long!"
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longhe of Emperor Ai of Jin children sang: "Shengping does not fill a dou—how can Longhe last long!"

sentences.zh: 桓公入石頭，陛下徒跣走。

translations.literal: "Lord Huan enters Shitou; Your Majesty runs barefoot."
translations.idiomatic: "Lord Huan enters Shitou; Your Majesty runs barefoot."

sentences.zh: 」帝聞而惡之，復改年曰興寧。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and hated it, and again changed the era name to Xingning.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heard and hated it, and again changed the era name to Xingning.

sentences.zh: 民復歌曰：「雖復改興寧，亦復無聊生。

translations.literal: The people again sang: "Though the name is changed to Xingning, still there is no way to live."
translations.idiomatic: The people again sang: "Though the name is changed to Xingning, still there is no way to live."

sentences.zh: 」哀帝尋崩，升平五年，穆帝崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai soon died; in the fifth year of Shengping Emperor Mu died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai soon died; in the fifth year of Shengping Emperor Mu died.

sentences.zh: 不滿斗，不至十年也。

translations.literal: Not filling a dou means not reaching ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Not filling a dou means not reaching ten years.

sentences.zh: 晉海西公太和中，民歌曰：「青青御路楊，白馬紫游韁。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era of the Deposed Emperor of Jin, the people sang: "Green, green—the poplars of the imperial road; white horse with purple bridle reins."
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era of the Deposed Emperor of Jin the people sang: "Green, green—the poplars of the imperial road; white horse with purple bridle reins."

sentences.zh: 汝非皇太子，那得甘露漿。

translations.literal: "You are not the Crown Prince—how can you obtain sweet-dew broth?"
translations.idiomatic: "You are not the Crown Prince—how can you obtain sweet-dew broth?"

sentences.zh: 」白者金行；

translations.literal: White is the element of metal;
translations.idiomatic: White is the element of metal;

sentences.zh: 馬者國族；

translations.literal: horse is the imperial clan;
translations.idiomatic: horse is the imperial clan;

sentences.zh: 紫為奪正之色，明以紫間朱也。

translations.literal: purple is the color of usurping the proper—clearly purple is interposed with vermilion.
translations.idiomatic: purple is the color of usurping the proper—clearly purple is interposed with vermilion.

sentences.zh: 海西公尋廢，三子非海西子，並死，縊以馬韁死之。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor was soon deposed; the three sons were not his sons—all died, strangled with horse reins.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor was soon deposed; the three sons were not his sons—all died, strangled with horse reins.

sentences.zh: 明日，南方獻甘露。

translations.literal: The next day the south presented sweet dew.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the south presented sweet dew.

sentences.zh: 太和末，童謠云：「犁牛耕御路，白門種小麥。

translations.literal: At the end of Taihe, a children's rhyme said: "A plow ox tills the imperial road; at White Gate they plant wheat."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Taihe a children's rhyme ran: "A plow ox tills the imperial road; at White Gate they plant wheat."

sentences.zh: 」及海西被廢，處吳，民犁耕其門前，以種小麥，如謠言。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor was deposed and dwelt in Wu, the people plowed before his gate and planted wheat, as the rhyme had said.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor was deposed and dwelt in Wu, the people plowed before his gate and planted wheat, as the rhyme had said.

sentences.zh: 晉海西公生皇子，百姓歌云：「鳳皇生一雛，天下莫不喜。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor of Jin had a prince born, the people sang: "The phoenix bears a chick—all under Heaven rejoice."
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor of Jin had a prince born, the people sang: "The phoenix bears a chick—all under Heaven rejoice."

sentences.zh: 本言是馬駒，今定成龍子。

translations.literal: "Originally said to be a horse colt—now fixed as a dragon's son."
translations.idiomatic: "Originally said to be a horse colt—now fixed as a dragon's son."

sentences.zh: 」其歌甚美，其旨甚微。

translations.literal: The song was very beautiful; its meaning was very subtle.
translations.idiomatic: The song was very beautiful; its meaning was very subtle.

sentences.zh: 海西公不男，使左右向龍與內侍接，生子以為己子。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor was not a man; he had attendants connect with eunuchs and bear a child, which he claimed as his own.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor was impotent; he had attendants connect with eunuchs and bear a child, which he claimed as his own.

sentences.zh: 桓石民為荊州，鎮上明，民忽歌曰「黃曇子」。

translations.literal: When Huan Shimin governed Jing Province and garrisoned Shangming, the people suddenly sang "Yellow Tan-zi."
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Shimin governed Jing Province and garrisoned Shangming, the people suddenly sang "Yellow Tan-zi."

sentences.zh: 曲終又曰：「黃曇英，揚州大佛來上明。

translations.literal: At the end of the tune it again said: "Yellow Tan-ying—the Great Buddha of Yang Province comes to Shangming."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the tune it again said: "Yellow Tan-ying—the Great Buddha of Yang Province comes to Shangming."

sentences.zh: 」頃之而石民死，王忱為荊州。

translations.literal: Before long Shimin died and Wang Chen became Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shimin died and Wang Chen became Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 「黃曇子」乃是王忱之字也。

translations.literal: "Yellow Tan-zi" was the style name of Wang Chen.
translations.idiomatic: "Yellow Tan-zi" was the style name of Wang Chen.

sentences.zh: 忱小字佛大，是「大佛來上明」也。

translations.literal: Chen's childhood name was Foda—this is "the Great Buddha comes to Shangming."
translations.idiomatic: Chen's childhood name was Foda—this is "the Great Buddha comes to Shangming."

sentences.zh: 太元末，京口謠曰：「黃雌雞，莫作雄父啼。

translations.literal: At the end of Taiyuan, a rhyme in Jingkou said: "Yellow hen, do not crow like a cock."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Taiyuan a rhyme in Jingkou ran: "Yellow hen, do not crow like a cock."

sentences.zh: 一旦去毛衣，衣被拉颯拪。

translations.literal: "One day you shed your feather coat; your garments are torn and stripped away."
translations.idiomatic: "One day you shed your feather coat; your garments are torn and stripped away."

sentences.zh: 」尋王恭起兵誅王國寶，旋為劉牢之所敗也。

translations.literal: Soon Wang Gong raised troops to execute Wang Guobao and was in turn defeated by Liu Lao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Gong raised troops to execute Wang Guobao and was in turn defeated by Liu Lao.

sentences.zh: 司馬道子於東府造土山，名曰靈秀山。

translations.literal: Sima Daozi built an earthen mountain in the Eastern Palace called Mount Lingxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daozi built an earthen mountain in the Eastern Palace called Mount Lingxiu.

sentences.zh: 無幾而孫恩作亂，再踐會稽。

translations.literal: Before long Sun En raised rebellion and twice overran Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sun En raised rebellion and twice overran Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 會稽，道子所封。

translations.literal: Kuaiji was Daozi's fief.
