translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji was Daozi's fief.

sentences.zh: 靈秀，恩之字也。

translations.literal: Lingxiu was En's style name.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxiu was En's style name.

sentences.zh: 庾楷鎮歷陽，民歌曰：「重羅犁，重羅犁，使君南上無還時。

translations.literal: When Yu Kai garrisoned Liyang, the people sang: "Heavy gauze plow, heavy gauze plow—the lord goes south and will not return."
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Kai garrisoned Liyang the people sang: "Heavy gauze plow, heavy gauze plow—the lord goes south and will not return."

sentences.zh: 」後楷南奔桓玄，為玄所誅。

translations.literal: Later Kai fled south to Huan Xuan and was executed by Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kai fled south to Huan Xuan and was executed by Xuan.

sentences.zh: 殷仲堪在荊州，童謠曰：「芒籠目，繩縛腹。

translations.literal: When Yin Zhongkan was in Jing Province, a children's rhyme said: "Awned basket eyes, rope bound around the belly."
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Zhongkan was in Jing Province a children's rhyme ran: "Awned basket eyes, rope bound around the belly."

sentences.zh: 殷當敗，桓當復。

translations.literal: "Yin shall fall; Huan shall rise again."
translations.idiomatic: "Yin shall fall; Huan shall rise again."

sentences.zh: 」無幾而仲堪敗，桓玄有荊州。

translations.literal: Before long Zhongkan was defeated and Huan Xuan held Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhongkan was defeated and Huan Xuan held Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 王恭鎮京口，舉兵誅王國寶，百姓謠云：「昔年食白飯，今年食麥䴸。

translations.literal: When Wang Gong garrisoned Jingkou and raised troops to execute Wang Guobao, the people sang: "In former years we ate white rice; this year we eat wheat bran."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Gong garrisoned Jingkou and raised troops to execute Wang Guobao, the people sang: "In former years we ate white rice; this year we eat wheat bran."

sentences.zh: 天公誅讁汝，教汝捻嚨喉。

translations.literal: "Heaven's lord will punish you and teach you to choke your throat."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven's lord will punish you and teach you to choke your throat."

sentences.zh: 嚨喉喝復喝，京口敗復敗。

translations.literal: "Throat choking again and again—Jingkou defeated again and again."
translations.idiomatic: "Throat choking again and again—Jingkou defeated again and again."

sentences.zh: 」「昔年食白飯」，言得志也。

translations.literal: "In former years we ate white rice" means having achieved one's ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: "In former years we ate white rice" means having achieved one's ambitions.

sentences.zh: 「今年食麥䴸」，䴸，粗穢，其精已去，明將敗也，天公將加譴讁而誅之也。

translations.literal: "This year we eat wheat bran"—bran is coarse and foul, its essence already gone—clearly he will be defeated; Heaven's lord will add punishment and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: "This year we eat wheat bran"—bran is coarse and foul, its essence already gone—clearly he will be defeated; Heaven's lord will add punishment and execute him.

sentences.zh: 「捻嚨喉」，氣不通，死之祥也。

translations.literal: "Choke the throat"—breath cannot pass; an omen of death.
translations.idiomatic: "Choke the throat"—breath cannot pass; an omen of death.

sentences.zh: 「敗復敗」，丁寧之辭也。

translations.literal: "Defeated again and again"—words of earnest warning.
translations.idiomatic: "Defeated again and again"—words of earnest warning.

sentences.zh: 恭尋死，京都大行咳疾，而喉並喝焉。

translations.literal: Gong soon died; the capital had a great outbreak of coughing illness, and throats all choked.
translations.idiomatic: Gong soon died; the capital had a great outbreak of coughing illness, and throats all choked.

sentences.zh: 王恭在京口，民間忽云：「黃頭小人欲作賊，阿公在城下，指縛得。

translations.literal: When Wang Gong was at Jingkou, the people suddenly said: "The yellow-headed little man wants to be a rebel; the old lord is below the wall—point and bind him."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Gong was at Jingkou the people suddenly said: "The yellow-headed little man wants to be a rebel; the old lord is below the wall—point and bind him."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「黃頭小人欲作亂，賴得金刀作蕃扞。

translations.literal: They also said: "The yellow-headed little man wants to make rebellion—thankfully the golden blade serves as a frontier guard."
translations.idiomatic: They also said: "The yellow-headed little man wants to make rebellion—thankfully the golden blade serves as a frontier guard."

sentences.zh: 」「黃」字上，「恭」字頭也。

translations.literal: Above the character "yellow" is the head of the character "Gong."
translations.idiomatic: Above the character "yellow" is the head of the character "Gong."

sentences.zh: 「小人」，「恭」字下也。

translations.literal: "Little man" is the lower part of the character "Gong."
translations.idiomatic: "Little man" is the lower part of the character "Gong."

sentences.zh: 尋如謠者言焉。

translations.literal: Soon it happened as the rhyme had said.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it happened as the rhyme had said.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安中，民忽作懊惱歌，其曲中有「草生可擥結，女兒可擥抱」之言。

translations.literal: In the Long'an era of Emperor An of Jin, the people suddenly made regret-and-vexation songs; in the tune were the words "when grass grows it can be gathered and tied; girls can be gathered and embraced."
translations.idiomatic: In the Long'an era of Emperor An of Jin the people suddenly made regret-and-vexation songs; in the tune were the words "when grass grows it can be gathered and tied; girls can be gathered and embraced."

sentences.zh: 桓玄既篡居天位，義旗以三月二日掃定京都，玄之宮女及逆黨之家子女伎妾，悉為軍賞。

translations.literal: After Huan Xuan usurped the throne, the righteous banner on the second day of the third month swept and settled the capital; Xuan's palace women and the daughters, performers, and concubines of rebel households all became military rewards.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan usurped the throne, the righteous banner on the second day of the third month swept and settled the capital; Xuan's palace women and the daughters, performers, and concubines of rebel households all became military rewards.

sentences.zh: 東及甌、越，北流淮、泗，皆人有所獲焉。

translations.literal: East to Ou and Yue, north flowing to the Huai and Si—all had people who gained something.
translations.idiomatic: East to Ou and Yue, north flowing to the Huai and Si—all had people who gained something.

sentences.zh: 時則草可結，事則女可抱，信矣。

translations.literal: At the time grass could be tied; in the event girls could be embraced—truly so.
translations.idiomatic: At the time grass could be tied; in the event girls could be embraced—truly so.

sentences.zh: 桓玄既篡，童謠曰：「草生及馬腹，烏啄桓玄目。

translations.literal: After Huan Xuan usurped, a children's rhyme said: "Grass grows to the horse's belly; crows peck at Huan Xuan's eyes."
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan usurped a children's rhyme ran: "Grass grows to the horse's belly; crows peck at Huan Xuan's eyes."

sentences.zh: 」及玄敗走至江陵，五月中誅，如其期焉。

translations.literal: When Xuan was defeated and fled to Jiangling, in the fifth month he was executed—just at the appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan was defeated and fled to Jiangling, in the fifth month he was executed—just at the appointed time.

sentences.zh: 桓玄時，民謠語云：「征鐘落地桓迸走。

translations.literal: In Huan Xuan's time, a folk rhyme said: "The privy bell falls to earth—Huan flees in panic."
translations.idiomatic: In Huan Xuan's time a folk rhyme ran: "The privy bell falls to earth—Huan flees in panic."

sentences.zh: 」征鐘，至穢之服，桓，四體之下稱。

translations.literal: Privy bell is the most foul garment; Huan is a name for the lower part of the body.
translations.idiomatic: Privy bell is the most foul garment; Huan is a name for the lower part of the body.

sentences.zh: 玄自下居上，猶征鐘之厠歌謠，下體之詠民口也。

translations.literal: Xuan rose from below to the top, like privy-bell latrine songs—verses of the lower body on the people's lips.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan rose from below to the top, like privy-bell latrine songs—verses of the lower body on the people's lips.

sentences.zh: 而云「落地」，墜地之祥，迸走之言，其驗明矣。

translations.literal: Yet it says "falls to earth"—an omen of falling to the ground; the words of fleeing in panic—the fulfillment is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it says "falls to earth"—an omen of falling to the ground; the words of fleeing in panic—the fulfillment is clear.

sentences.zh: 司馬元顯時，民謠詩云：「當有十一口，當為兵所傷。

translations.literal: In Sima Yuanxian's time, a folk rhyme-poem said: "There shall be eleven mouths—they shall be wounded by soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: In Sima Yuanxian's time a folk rhyme-poem ran: "There shall be eleven mouths—they shall be wounded by soldiers."

sentences.zh: 木亘當北度，走入浩浩鄉。

translations.literal: "Mu and huan shall cross north and flee into the vast homeland."
translations.idiomatic: "Mu and huan shall cross north and flee into the vast homeland."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「金刀既以刻，娓娓金城中。

translations.literal: It also said: "The golden blade is already carved—flourishing within the golden city."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "The golden blade is already carved—flourishing within the golden city."

sentences.zh: 」此詩云襄陽道人竺曇林所作，多所道，行於世。

translations.literal: This poem says it was composed by the Daoist Zhu Tanlin of Xiangyang; it spoke of many things and circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: This poem says it was composed by the Daoist Zhu Tanlin of Xiangyang; it spoke of many things and circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 孟顗釋之曰，「十一口」者，玄字象也。

translations.literal: Meng Yan explained it: "Eleven mouths" is the image of the character Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yan explained it: "Eleven mouths" is the image of the character Xuan.

sentences.zh: 「木亘」，桓也。

translations.literal: "Mu and huan" is Huan.
translations.idiomatic: "Mu and huan" is Huan.

sentences.zh: 桓氏當悉走入關、洛，故云「浩浩鄉」也。

translations.literal: The Huan clan would all flee into Guan and Luo—therefore it says "vast homeland."
translations.idiomatic: The Huan clan would all flee into Guan and Luo—therefore it says "vast homeland."

sentences.zh: 「金刀」，劉也。

translations.literal: "Golden blade" is Liu.
translations.idiomatic: "Golden blade" is Liu.

sentences.zh: 倡義諸公，皆多姓劉。

translations.literal: The lords who raised the righteous cause were mostly surnamed Liu.
translations.idiomatic: The lords who raised the righteous cause were mostly surnamed Liu.

sentences.zh: 「娓娓」，美盛貌也。

translations.literal: "Flourishing" is the appearance of beauty and splendor.
translations.idiomatic: "Flourishing" is the appearance of beauty and splendor.

sentences.zh: 桓玄得志，童謠曰：「長干巷，巷長干。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan got his way, a children's rhyme said: "Changgan Lane—lane Changgan."
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan got his way a children's rhyme ran: "Changgan Lane—lane Changgan."

sentences.zh: 今年殺郎君，明年斬諸桓。

translations.literal: "This year kill the young lord; next year behead all the Huans."
translations.idiomatic: "This year kill the young lord; next year behead all the Huans."

sentences.zh: 」及玄走而諸桓悉誅焉。

translations.literal: When Xuan fled, all the Huans were executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan fled, all the Huans were executed.

sentences.zh: 郎君，司馬元顯也。

translations.literal: The young lord is Sima Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: The young lord is Sima Yuanxian.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙初，童謠曰：「官家養蘆化成荻，蘆生不止自成積。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi of Emperor An of Jin, a children's rhyme said: "The court raises reeds that turn into rushes; reeds grow without cease and form heaps of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yixi of Emperor An of Jin a children's rhyme ran: "The court raises reeds that turn into rushes; reeds grow without cease and form heaps of themselves."

sentences.zh: 」其時官養盧龍，寵以金紫，奉以名州，養之已極，而不能懷我好音，舉兵內伐，遂成讎敵也。

translations.literal: At that time the court raised Lu Long, favored him with gold and purple, granted him a famous province, and raised him to the utmost—yet he could not cherish our goodwill, raised troops for internal attack, and became a sworn enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court raised Lu Long, favored him with gold and purple, granted him a famous province, and raised him to the utmost—yet he could not cherish our goodwill, raised troops for internal attack, and became a sworn enemy.

sentences.zh: 「蘆生不止自成積」，及盧龍作亂，時人追思童謠，惡其有成積之言。

translations.literal: "Reeds grow without cease and form heaps of themselves"—when Lu Long raised rebellion, people of the time recalled the children's rhyme and hated its words about forming heaps.
translations.idiomatic: "Reeds grow without cease and form heaps of themselves"—when Lu Long raised rebellion, people of the time recalled the children's rhyme and hated its words about forming heaps.

sentences.zh: 識者曰：「芟夷蘊崇之，又行火焉，是草之窮也。

translations.literal: Those who understood said: "Cut down what has been piled up, and again apply fire—this is the end of grass."
translations.idiomatic: Those who understood said: "Cut down what has been piled up, and again apply fire—this is the end of grass."

sentences.zh: 伐斫以成積，又以為薪，亦蘆荻之終也。

translations.literal: Cut and chop to form heaps, then use them as fuel—this too is the end of reeds and rushes.
translations.idiomatic: Cut and chop to form heaps, then use them as fuel—this too is the end of reeds and rushes.

sentences.zh: 其盛既極，亦將芟夷而為積焉。

translations.literal: When its flourishing has reached its limit, it too will be cut down and piled up.
translations.idiomatic: When its flourishing had reached its limit, it too would be cut down and piled up.

sentences.zh: 」龍既窮其兵勢，盛其舟艦，卒以滅亡，僵屍如積焉。

translations.literal: Long exhausted his military power and gloried in his river fleets, yet in the end perished—corpses piled like heaps.
translations.idiomatic: Long exhausted his military power and gloried in his river fleets, yet in the end perished—corpses piled like heaps.

sentences.zh: 盧龍據有廣州，民間謠云：「蘆生漫漫竟天半。

translations.literal: When Lu Long held Guang Province, a folk rhyme said: "Reeds grow vast and reach halfway to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Long held Guang Province a folk rhyme ran: "Reeds grow vast and reach halfway to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」後擁有上流數州之地，內逼京輦，應「天半」之言。

translations.literal: Later he held several provinces of the upper reaches and pressed inward on the capital region—fulfilling the words "halfway to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Later he held several provinces of the upper reaches and pressed inward on the capital region—fulfilling the words "halfway to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 義熙三年中，小兒相逢於道，輒舉其兩手曰「盧健健」，次曰「鬭嘆，鬭嘆」，末復曰「翁年老，翁年老」。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yixi, when children met on the road they would raise both hands and say "Lu jian-jian," next say "Fight and sigh, fight and sigh," and finally say "The old lord is aged, the old lord is aged."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yixi, when children met on the road they would raise both hands and say "Lu jian-jian," next say "Fight and sigh, fight and sigh," and finally say "The old lord is aged, the old lord is aged."

sentences.zh: 當時莫知所謂。

translations.literal: At the time no one knew what it meant.
translations.idiomatic: At the time no one knew what it meant.

sentences.zh: 其後盧龍內逼，舟艦蓋川，「健健」之謂也。

translations.literal: Afterward Lu Long pressed inward and river fleets covered the streams—this is what "jian-jian" meant.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Lu Long pressed inward and river fleets covered the streams—this is what "jian-jian" meant.

sentences.zh: 既至查浦，屢剋期欲與官鬭，「鬭嘆」之應也。

translations.literal: When he reached Zhapu he repeatedly set dates to fight the officials—the fulfillment of "fight and sigh."
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Zhapu he repeatedly set dates to fight the officials—the fulfillment of "fight and sigh."

sentences.zh: 「翁年老」，羣公有期頤之慶，知妖逆之徒，自然消殄也。

translations.literal: "The old lord is aged"—the lords had the blessing of a hundred years and knew the demonic rebels would naturally be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: "The old lord is aged"—the lords had the blessing of a hundred years and knew the demonic rebels would naturally be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 其時復有謠言曰：「盧橙橙，逐水流，東風忽如起，那得入石頭。

translations.literal: At that time there was again a rhyme that said: "Lu cheng-cheng, chasing the water's flow—if the east wind suddenly rises, how can he enter Shitou?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was again a rhyme that ran: "Lu cheng-cheng, chasing the water's flow—if the east wind suddenly rises, how can he enter Shitou?"

sentences.zh: 」盧龍果敗，不得入石頭。

translations.literal: Lu Long was indeed defeated and could not enter Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Long was indeed defeated and could not enter Shitou.

sentences.zh: 昔溫嶠令郭景純卜己與庾亮吉凶。

translations.literal: Formerly Wen Jiao had Guo Jingchun divinate the fortune of himself and Yu Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Wen Jiao had Guo Jingchun divinate the fortune of himself and Yu Liang.

sentences.zh: 景純云「元吉」。

translations.literal: Jingchun said "originally auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Jingchun said "originally auspicious."

sentences.zh: 」嶠語亮：「景純每筮，當是不敢盡言。

translations.literal: Jiao said to Liang: "Whenever Jingchun divines, he surely dares not speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao said to Liang: "Whenever Jingchun divines, he surely dares not speak fully.

sentences.zh: 吾等與國家同安危而曰元吉，事有成也。

translations.literal: We share the state's safety and peril, yet he says originally auspicious—the affair will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: We share the state's safety and peril, yet he says originally auspicious—the affair will succeed."

sentences.zh: 」於是協同討滅王敦。

translations.literal: Thereupon they joined together to campaign and destroy Wang Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they joined together to campaign and destroy Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 苻堅中，童謠曰：「阿堅連牽三十年，後若欲敗時，當在江湖邊。

translations.literal: In Fu Jian's time, a children's rhyme said: "Ah Jian linked and led for thirty years—when he later wishes to be defeated, it will be beside rivers and lakes."
translations.idiomatic: In Fu Jian's time a children's rhyme ran: "Ah Jian linked and led for thirty years—when he later wishes to be defeated, it will be beside rivers and lakes."

sentences.zh: 」後堅敗於淝水，在偽位凡三十年。

translations.literal: Later Jian was defeated at the Fei River; on the false throne altogether thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jian was defeated at the Fei River; on the false throne altogether thirty years.

sentences.zh: 苻堅中，謠語云：「河水清復清，苻詔死新城。

translations.literal: In Fu Jian's time, a rhyme said: "The river water clears and clears again—Fu Zhao dies at New City."
translations.idiomatic: In Fu Jian's time a rhyme ran: "The river water clears and clears again—Fu Zhao dies at New City."

sentences.zh: 」堅為姚萇所殺，死於新城。

translations.literal: Jian was killed by Yao Chang and died at New City.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was killed by Yao Chang and died at New City.

sentences.zh: 苻堅中，歌云：「魚羊田斗當滅秦。

translations.literal: In Fu Jian's time, a song said: "Fish and sheep, field and dou—Qin shall be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: In Fu Jian's time a song ran: "Fish and sheep, field and dou—Qin shall be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 」「魚羊」，鮮也。

translations.literal: "Fish and sheep" is Xian—the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: "Fish and sheep" is Xian—the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 「田斗」，卑也。

translations.literal: "Field and dou" is bei—lowly.
translations.idiomatic: "Field and dou" is bei—lowly.

sentences.zh: 堅自號秦，言滅之者鮮卑也。

translations.literal: Jian styled himself Qin—it means the destroyer is the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Jian styled himself Qin—it means the destroyer is the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 其羣臣諫堅，令盡誅鮮卑。

translations.literal: His ministers remonstrated with Jian, urging him to execute all the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers remonstrated with Jian, urging him to execute all the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 堅不從。

translations.literal: Jian did not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: Jian did not heed them.

sentences.zh: 及淮南敗還，為慕容沖所攻，亡奔姚萇，身死國滅。

translations.literal: When he was defeated at Huainan and returned, he was attacked by Murong Chong, fled to Yao Chang, and died—his person perished and his state was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When he was defeated at Huainan and returned, he was attacked by Murong Chong, fled to Yao Chang, and died—his person perished and his state was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 毛蟲之孽

translations.literal: Calamities of hairy creatures
translations.idiomatic: Calamities of Hairy Creatures

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康六年，南陽送兩足虎，此毛蟲之孽也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, Nanyang presented a two-legged tiger—this was a calamity of hairy creatures.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, Nanyang presented a two-legged tiger—this was a calamity of hairy creatures.

sentences.zh: 識者為其文曰：「武形有虧，金虎失儀，聖主應天，斯異何為。

translations.literal: Those who understood composed a text for it: "The martial form is flawed; the golden tiger loses its proper bearing; the sage lord responds to Heaven—why this anomaly?"
translations.idiomatic: Those who understood composed a text for it: "The martial form is flawed; the golden tiger loses its proper bearing; the sage lord responds to Heaven—why this anomaly?"

sentences.zh: 」言非亂也。

translations.literal: It means not rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: It means not rebellion.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「足少者，下不勝任也。

translations.literal: The Tradition of Changes of Jing Fang says: "When feet are few, the lower cannot bear the burden."
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition of Changes of Jing Fang says: "When feet are few, the lower cannot bear the burden."

sentences.zh: 」干寶曰：「虎者陰精，而居于陽。

translations.literal: Gan Bao says: "The tiger is yin essence yet dwells in yang.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao says: "The tiger is yin essence yet dwells in yang.

sentences.zh: 金獸也。

translations.literal: It is a creature of metal.
translations.idiomatic: It is a creature of metal.

sentences.zh: 南陽，火名也。

translations.literal: Nanyang is a name of fire.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang is a name of fire.

sentences.zh: 金精入火，而失其形，王室亂之妖也。

translations.literal: Metal essence enters fire and loses its form—an omen of disorder in the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Metal essence enters fire and loses its form—an omen of disorder in the royal house.

sentences.zh: 六，水數，言水數既極，火慝得作，而金受其敗也。

translations.literal: Six is the number of water—it means the water number has reached its limit, fire's evil can act, and metal receives defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Six is the number of water—it means the water number has reached its limit, fire's evil can act, and metal receives defeat.

sentences.zh: 至元康九年，始殺太子，距此十四年。

translations.literal: By the ninth year of Yuankang the Crown Prince was first killed—fourteen years from this.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth year of Yuankang the Crown Prince was first killed—fourteen years from this.

sentences.zh: 二七十四，火始終相乘之數也。

translations.literal: Two times seven is fourteen—the number of fire's beginning and end multiplied together.
translations.idiomatic: Two times seven is fourteen—the number of fire's beginning and end multiplied together.

sentences.zh: 自帝受命，至愍懷之廢，凡三十五年。」

translations.literal: From the Emperor receiving the Mandate to Minhuai's deposition, altogether thirty-five years."
translations.idiomatic: From the Emperor receiving the Mandate to Minhuai's deposition, altogether thirty-five years."

sentences.zh: 太康九年，荊州獻兩足玃。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taikang, Jing Province presented a two-legged ape.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taikang, Jing Province presented a two-legged ape.

sentences.zh: 太康七年十一月丙辰，四角獸見于河間，河間王顒獲以獻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day bingchen of the seventh year of Taikang, a four-horned beast appeared in Hejian; the Prince of Hejian Sima Yong captured and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day bingchen of the seventh year of Taikang, a four-horned beast appeared in Hejian; the Prince of Hejian Sima Yong captured and presented it.

sentences.zh: 角，兵象也。

translations.literal: Horns are the image of arms.
translations.idiomatic: Horns are the image of arms.

sentences.zh: 董仲舒以四角為四方之象。

translations.literal: Dong Zhongshu took four horns as the image of the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu took four horns as the image of the four directions.

sentences.zh: 後河間王數連四方之兵，作為亂階，殆其應也。

translations.literal: Later the Prince of Hejian repeatedly linked armies from the four directions and made the steps of rebellion—perhaps the corresponding response.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Prince of Hejian repeatedly linked armies from the four directions and made the steps of rebellion—perhaps the corresponding response.

sentences.zh: 晉懷帝永嘉五年，偃鼠出延陵，此毛蟲之孽也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongjia of Emperor Huai of Jin, a mole-rat appeared at Yanling—this was a calamity of hairy creatures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongjia of Emperor Huai of Jin, a mole-rat appeared at Yanling—this was a calamity of hairy creatures.

sentences.zh: 郭景純筮之曰：「此郡東之縣，當有妖人欲稱制者，亦尋自死矣。

translations.literal: Guo Jingchun divined it and said: "In a county east of this commandery there will be a demonic man wishing to claim regency—he too will soon die of himself."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jingchun divined it and said: "In a county east of this commandery there will be a demonic man wishing to claim regency—he too will soon die of himself."

sentences.zh: 」其後吳興徐馥作亂，殺太守袁琇，馥亦時滅，是其應也。

translations.literal: Afterward Xu Fu of Wuxing raised rebellion, killed the Administrator Yuan Xiu, and Fu too was soon destroyed—the corresponding response.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Xu Fu of Wuxing raised rebellion, killed the Administrator Yuan Xiu, and Fu too was soon destroyed—the corresponding response.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸和六年正月丁巳，會州郡秀孝於樂賢堂，有麏見於前，獲之。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi of the first month of the sixth year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng of Jin, the court assembled the outstanding and filial from the provinces and commanderies at the Hall for Delighting in Worthies; a roe deer appeared before them and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi of the first month of the sixth year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng of Jin, the court assembled the outstanding and filial from the provinces and commanderies at the Hall for Delighting in Worthies; a roe deer appeared before them and was captured.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：「夫秀孝，天下之彥士，樂賢堂，所以樂養賢也。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: "The outstanding and filial are the finest scholars under Heaven; the Hall for Delighting in Worthies is where worthies are delighted and nurtured.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng says: "The outstanding and filial are the finest scholars under Heaven; the Hall for Delighting in Worthies is where worthies are delighted and nurtured.

sentences.zh: 晉自喪亂以後，風教凌夷，秀無策試之才，孝乏四行之實。

translations.literal: Since the disorders Jin's customs and teaching have declined; the outstanding lack talent for policy examination, the filial lack the substance of the four virtues.
translations.idiomatic: Since the disorders Jin's customs and teaching have declined; the outstanding lack talent for policy examination, the filial lack the substance of the four virtues.

sentences.zh: 麏興於前，或斯故乎。」

translations.literal: A roe deer rising before them—is it for this reason."
translations.idiomatic: A roe deer rising before them—is it for this reason."

sentences.zh: 晉哀帝隆和元年十月甲申，有麈入東海第。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on the day jiashen of the first year of Longhe of Emperor Ai of Jin, an elk entered the residence of the Prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on the day jiashen of the first year of Longhe of Emperor Ai of Jin, an elk entered the residence of the Prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 百姓讙言曰：「主入東海第。

translations.literal: The common people shouted in joy: "The lord enters the residence of Donghai."
translations.idiomatic: The common people shouted in joy: "The lord enters the residence of Donghai."

sentences.zh: 」識者怪之。

translations.literal: Those who understood found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Those who understood found it strange.

sentences.zh: 及海西廢為東海王，先送此第。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor was deposed and made Prince of Donghai, he was first sent to this residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor was deposed and made Prince of Donghai, he was first sent to this residence.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武太元十三年四月癸巳，礿祠畢，有兔行廟堂上。

translations.literal: On the day guisi of the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, when the yue sacrifice was completed, a rabbit walked on the temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guisi of the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, when the yue sacrifice was completed, a rabbit walked on the temple hall.

sentences.zh: 兔，野物也，而集宗廟之堂，不祥莫甚焉。

translations.literal: The rabbit is a wild creature, yet it gathered in the hall of the ancestral temple—nothing could be more inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The rabbit is a wild creature, yet it gathered in the hall of the ancestral temple—nothing could be more inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十四年二月，雍州送六足麞，刺史武陵王表為祥瑞。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, Yong Province presented a six-legged roe deer; the Inspector, the Prince of Wuling, memorialized it as an auspicious portent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, Yong Province presented a six-legged roe deer; the Inspector, the Prince of Wuling, memorialized it as an auspicious portent.

sentences.zh: 此毛蟲之孽。

translations.literal: This was a calamity of hairy creatures.
translations.idiomatic: This was a calamity of hairy creatures.

sentences.zh: 宋順帝昇明元年，象三頭度蔡洲，暴稻穀及園野。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming of Emperor Shun of Song, three elephants crossed Cai Isle and ravaged rice grain and gardens and fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengming of Emperor Shun of Song, three elephants crossed Cai Isle and ravaged rice grain and gardens and fields.

sentences.zh: 犬禍

translations.literal: Canine disasters
translations.idiomatic: Canine Disasters

sentences.zh: 公孫淵家有犬冠幘絳衣上屋，此犬禍也。

translations.literal: In Gongsun Yuan's house a dog wore a kerchief and scarlet clothes and went up on the roof—this was a canine disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In Gongsun Yuan's house a dog wore a kerchief and scarlet clothes and went up on the roof—this was a canine disaster.

sentences.zh: 屋上亢陽高危之地。

translations.literal: The roof is a place of excessive yang, high and perilous.
translations.idiomatic: The roof is a place of excessive yang, high and perilous.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，淵亢陽無上，偷自尊高，狗而冠者也。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seems to say: Yuan is excessively yang without limit, stealthily elevating himself in arrogance—a dog wearing a cap.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seems to say: Yuan is excessively yang without limit, stealthily elevating himself in arrogance—a dog wearing a cap.

sentences.zh: 及自立為燕王，果為魏所滅。

translations.literal: When he established himself as King of Yan, he was indeed destroyed by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When he established himself as King of Yan, he was indeed destroyed by Wei.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「君不正，臣欲篡，厥妖狗出朝門。」

translations.literal: The Tradition of Changes of Jing Fang says: "When the ruler is not upright and ministers wish to usurp, the anomaly is a dog coming out the court gate."
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition of Changes of Jing Fang says: "When the ruler is not upright and ministers wish to usurp, the anomaly is a dog coming out the court gate."

sentences.zh: 魏侍中應璩在直廬，欻見一白狗，問眾人無見者。

translations.literal: The Wei Palace Attendant Ying Qu, on duty in the lodge, suddenly saw a white dog; he asked the others and none had seen it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Palace Attendant Ying Qu, on duty in the lodge, suddenly saw a white dog; he asked the others and none had seen it.

sentences.zh: 踰年卒。

translations.literal: After a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he died.

sentences.zh: 近犬禍也。

translations.literal: This was a recent canine disaster.
translations.idiomatic: This was a recent canine disaster.

sentences.zh: 諸葛恪征淮南歸，將朝會，犬銜引其衣。

translations.literal: When Zhuge Ke returned from campaigning in Huainan and was about to attend court assembly, a dog seized and pulled his garment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Ke returned from campaigning in Huainan and was about to attend court assembly, a dog seized and pulled his garment.

sentences.zh: 恪曰：「犬不欲我行乎？

translations.literal: Ke said: "Does the dog not wish me to go?"
translations.idiomatic: Ke said: "Does the dog not wish me to go?"

sentences.zh: 」還坐，有頃復起，犬又銜衣。

translations.literal: He returned to his seat; after a while he rose again, and the dog again seized his garment.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to his seat; after a while he rose again, and the dog again seized his garment.

sentences.zh: 乃令逐犬。

translations.literal: He then ordered the dog driven away.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the dog driven away.

sentences.zh: 遂升車入而被害。

translations.literal: He then mounted his carriage and entered, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He then mounted his carriage and entered, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康九年，幽州有犬，鼻行地三百餘步。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, in You Province there was a dog that walked on its nose for more than three hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, in You Province there was a dog that walked on its nose for more than three hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康中，吳郡婁縣民家聞地中有犬聲，掘視得雌雄各一。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of Jin, a commoner's household in Lou County of Wu Commandery heard dog sounds in the earth; digging they found one male and one female.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of Jin, a commoner's household in Lou County of Wu Commandery heard dog sounds in the earth; digging they found one male and one female.

sentences.zh: 還置窟中，覆以磨石，宿昔失所在。

translations.literal: They returned them to the burrow, covered it with a millstone, and overnight they vanished.
translations.idiomatic: They returned them to the burrow, covered it with a millstone, and overnight they vanished.

sentences.zh: 元帝太興中，吳郡府舍又得二物頭如此。

translations.literal: In the Taixing era of Emperor Yuan, the Wu Commandery government offices again obtained two creatures' heads like this.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taixing era of Emperor Yuan, the Wu Commandery government offices again obtained two creatures' heads like this.

sentences.zh: 其後太守張茂為吳興兵所殺。

translations.literal: Afterward the Administrator Zhang Mao was killed by Wuxing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Administrator Zhang Mao was killed by Wuxing troops.

sentences.zh: 案夏鼎志曰：「掘地得狗名曰賈。

translations.literal: Examining the Record of the Xia Cauldron, it says: "Digging earth and obtaining a dog is called Jia."
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Record of the Xia Cauldron, it says: "Digging earth and obtaining a dog is called Jia."

sentences.zh: 」尸子曰：「地中有犬，名曰地狼。

translations.literal: Master Shi says: "In the earth there is a dog called the earth wolf."
translations.idiomatic: Master Shi says: "In the earth there is a dog called the earth wolf."

sentences.zh: 」同實而異名也。

translations.literal: The same substance with different names.
translations.idiomatic: The same substance with different names.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永興元年，丹陽內史朱逵家犬生三子，皆無頭，後逵為揚州刺史曹武所殺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxing of Emperor Hui of Jin, the Administrator of Danyang Zhu Kui's dog bore three pups, all headless; later Kui was killed by the Inspector of Yang Province Cao Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongxing of Emperor Hui of Jin, the Administrator of Danyang Zhu Kui's dog bore three pups, all headless; later Kui was killed by the Inspector of Yang Province Cao Wu.

sentences.zh: 晉孝懷帝永嘉五年，吳郡嘉興張林家狗人言云：「天下人餓死。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongjia of Emperor Xiaohuai of Jin, the dog at Zhang Lin's house in Jiaxing of Wu Commandery spoke in human words: "All the people under Heaven will starve to death."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongjia of Emperor Xiaohuai of Jin, the dog at Zhang Lin's house in Jiaxing of Wu Commandery spoke in human words: "All the people under Heaven will starve to death."

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安初，吳郡治下狗恒夜吠，聚高橋上。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Long'an of Emperor An of Jin, dogs under the Wu Commandery administration constantly barked at night, gathering on the high bridge.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Long'an of Emperor An of Jin, dogs under the Wu Commandery administration constantly barked at night, gathering on the high bridge.

sentences.zh: 人家狗有限，而吠聲甚眾。

translations.literal: Household dogs were limited in number, yet the barking was very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Household dogs were limited in number, yet the barking was very numerous.

sentences.zh: 或有夜出覘之者，云一狗假有兩三頭，皆前向亂吠。

translations.literal: Some who went out at night to observe said one dog seemed to have two or three heads, all facing forward and barking wildly.
translations.idiomatic: Some who went out at night to observe said one dog seemed to have two or three heads, all facing forward and barking wildly.

sentences.zh: 無幾，孫恩亂於吳會。

translations.literal: Before long Sun En raised disorder in Wu and Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sun En raised disorder in Wu and Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 桓玄將拜楚王，已設拜席，羣官陪位，玄未及出，有狗來便其席，萬眾暀候，莫不驚怪。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan was about to be invested as King of Chu, the investiture mat was already set and the hundred officials attended in place; before Xuan could come out, a dog came and soiled his mat—the myriad masses waited in silence, and all were startled.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan was about to be invested as King of Chu, the investiture mat was already set and the hundred officials attended in place; before Xuan could come out, a dog came and soiled his mat—the myriad masses waited in silence, and all were startled.

sentences.zh: 玄性猜暴，竟無言者，逐狗改席而已。

translations.literal: Xuan was suspicious and violent by nature; in the end no one spoke—they merely drove off the dog and changed the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was suspicious and violent by nature; in the end no one spoke—they merely drove off the dog and changed the mat.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝永初二年，京邑有狗人言。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu of Emperor Wu of Song, in the capital there was a dog that spoke in human words.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongchu of Emperor Wu of Song, in the capital there was a dog that spoke in human words.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉二十九年，吳興東遷孟慧度婢蠻與狗通好如夫妻彌年。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen, the bondwoman Man of Meng Huidu in Dongqian of Wuxing consorted with a dog as husband and wife for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen, the bondwoman Man of Meng Huidu in Dongqian of Wuxing consorted with a dog as husband and wife for a full year.

sentences.zh: 孝武孝建初，顏竣為左衞，於省內聞犬子聲在地中，掘焉得烏犬子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiaowu, Yan Jun was Left Guard; within the office he heard the sound of a puppy in the earth, dug, and obtained a black puppy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiaowu, Yan Jun was Left Guard; within the office he heard the sound of a puppy in the earth, dug, and obtained a black puppy.

sentences.zh: 養久之，後自死。

translations.literal: He raised it for a long time; later it died of itself.
translations.idiomatic: He raised it for a long time; later it died of itself.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，晉安王子勛稱偽號於尋陽，柴桑有狗與女人交，三日不分離。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming, Prince of Jin'an Zixun claimed a false title at Xunyang; at Chaisang a dog coupled with a woman and for three days would not separate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming, Prince of Jin'an Zixun claimed a false title at Xunyang; at Chaisang a dog coupled with a woman and for three days would not separate.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始中，秣陵張僧護家犬生豕子。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era of Emperor Ming, the dog at Zhang Senghu's house in Moling bore a piglet.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era of Emperor Ming, the dog at Zhang Senghu's house in Moling bore a piglet.

sentences.zh: 白眚白祥

translations.literal: White disasters and white portents
translations.idiomatic: White Disasters and White Portents

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康十年，洛陽宮西宜秋里石生地中，始高三尺，如香鑪形，後如傴人，盤薄不可掘。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, in Yiqiu Lane west of the Luoyang palace stone grew from the earth; at first three chi high, shaped like an incense burner, later like a hunchback—twining and impossible to dig up.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, in Yiqiu Lane west of the Luoyang palace stone grew from the earth; at first three chi high, shaped like an incense burner, later like a hunchback—twining and impossible to dig up.

sentences.zh: 案劉向說，此白眚也。

translations.literal: Examining Liu Xiang's explanation, this was a white disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Liu Xiang's explanation, this was a white disaster.

sentences.zh: 明年，宮車晏駕，王室始騷，卒以亂亡。

translations.literal: The next year the imperial carriage departed at dusk; the royal house first grew turbulent and in the end perished in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the imperial carriage departed at dusk; the royal house first grew turbulent and in the end perished in disorder.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「石立如人，庶人為天下雄。

translations.literal: The Tradition of Changes of Jing Fang says: "Stone stands like a man—the common people become lords of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition of Changes of Jing Fang says: "Stone stands like a man—the common people become lords of the realm."

sentences.zh: 」此近之矣。

translations.literal: This came close to it.
translations.idiomatic: This came close to it.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康初，地生毛，近白眚也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiankang of Emperor Cheng of Jin, hair grew from the earth—a recent white disaster.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin hair grew from the earth—a recent white disaster.

sentences.zh: 孫盛以為民勞之異。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng took it as an anomaly of the people's exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng took it as an anomaly of the people's exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 是後胡滅而中原向化，將相皆甘心焉。

translations.literal: After this the Hu were destroyed and the Central Plains turned toward civilization; generals and chancellors all gave their hearts to it.
translations.idiomatic: After this the Hu were destroyed and the Central Plains turned toward civilization; generals and chancellors all gave their hearts to it.

sentences.zh: 於是方鎮屢革，邊戍仍遷，皆擁帶部曲，動有萬數，其間征伐徵賦，役無寧歲，天下擾動，民以疲怨。

translations.literal: Thereupon regional commands were repeatedly reformed and frontier garrisons continually redeployed; all held personal followings numbering in the tens of thousands; meanwhile campaigns and levies went on year after year without respite—the realm was disturbed and the people grew weary and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon regional commands were repeatedly reformed and frontier garrisons continually redeployed; all held personal followings numbering in the tens of thousands; meanwhile campaigns and levies went on year after year without respite—the realm was disturbed and the people grew weary and resentful.

sentences.zh: 咸康三年六月，地生毛。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Xiankang, hair grew from the earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Xiankang hair grew from the earth.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武太元二年五月，京都地生毛。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, hair grew from the earth in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin hair grew from the earth in the capital.

sentences.zh: 至四年而氐賊攻襄陽，圍彭城，向廣陵，征戍仍出，兵連不解。

translations.literal: By the fourth year the Di rebels attacked Xiangyang, besieged Pengcheng, and advanced toward Guangling; expeditions and garrisons went out continually and warfare never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth year the Di rebels attacked Xiangyang, besieged Pengcheng, and advanced toward Guangling; expeditions and garrisons went out continually and warfare never ceased.

sentences.zh: 太元十四年四月，京都地生毛。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year of Taiyuan, hair grew from the earth in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year of Taiyuan hair grew from the earth in the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時苻堅滅後，經略多事。

translations.literal: At this time after Fu Jian's destruction, securing the realm involved many affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, after Fu Jian's destruction, securing the realm involved many affairs.

sentences.zh: 太元十七年四月，地生毛。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventeenth year of Taiyuan, hair grew from the earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the seventeenth year of Taiyuan hair grew from the earth.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安四年四月乙未，地生毛，或白或黑。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei of the fourth month of the fourth year of Long'an of Emperor An of Jin, hair grew from the earth, some white and some black.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiwei of the fourth month of the fourth year of Long'an under Emperor An of Jin hair grew from the earth, some white and some black.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝元興三年五月，江陵地生毛。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Yuanxing of Emperor An of Jin, hair grew from the earth at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Yuanxing under Emperor An of Jin hair grew from the earth at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 是後江陵見襲，交戰者數矣。

translations.literal: After this Jiangling was attacked several times in battle.
translations.idiomatic: After this Jiangling was attacked several times in battle.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙三年三月，地生白毛。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Yixi of Emperor An of Jin, white hair grew from the earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin white hair grew from the earth.

sentences.zh: 義熙十年三月，地生白毛。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year of Yixi, white hair grew from the earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the tenth year of Yixi white hair grew from the earth.

sentences.zh: 明年，王旅西討司馬休之。

translations.literal: The next year the royal army campaigned west against Sima Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the royal army campaigned west against Sima Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 又明年，北掃關、洛。

translations.literal: The year after that, they swept north through Guan and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that they swept north through Guan and Luo.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝青龍三年正月乙亥，隕石于壽光。

translations.literal: On the day yihai of the first month of the third year of Qinglong of Emperor Ming of Wei, a meteorite fell at Shouguang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai of the first month of the third year of Qinglong under Emperor Ming of Wei a meteorite fell at Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 按左氏傳，隕石，星也。

translations.literal: Examining the Zuo Tradition, a falling stone is a star.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Zuo Tradition, a falling stone is a star.

sentences.zh: 劉歆說曰：「庶民，惟星隕於宋者，象宋襄公將得諸侯而不終也。

translations.literal: Liu Xin's explanation says: "The common people—only when a star fell in Song did it symbolize Duke Xiang of Song about to gain the feudal lords yet not reaching the end."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin's explanation says: "The common people—only when a star fell in Song did it symbolize Duke Xiang of Song about to gain the feudal lords yet not reaching the end."

sentences.zh: 」秦始皇時有隕石。

translations.literal: In the time of the First Emperor of Qin there was a falling meteorite.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of the First Emperor of Qin there was a falling meteorite.

sentences.zh: 班固以為石陰類，又白祥，臣將危君。

translations.literal: Ban Gu held that stone is of the yin kind, and also a white portent—ministers will endanger the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu held that stone is of the yin kind, and also a white portent—ministers will endanger the ruler.

sentences.zh: 是後司馬氏得政。

translations.literal: After this the house of Sima obtained government.
translations.idiomatic: After this the house of Sima obtained government.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康五年五月丁巳，隕石于溫及河陽各二。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi of the fifth month of the fifth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, meteorites fell at Wen and Heyang, two at each place.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi of the fifth month of the fifth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin meteorites fell at Wen and Heyang, two at each place.

sentences.zh: 太康六年正月，隕石于溫三。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Taikang, three meteorites fell at Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year of Taikang three meteorites fell at Wen.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸和八年五月，星隕于肥鄉一。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng of Jin, one star fell at Feixiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng of Jin one star fell at Feixiang.

sentences.zh: 咸和九年正月，隕石于涼州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year of Xianhe, a meteorite fell in Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year of Xianhe a meteorite fell in Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮五鳳二年五月，陽羨縣離里山大石自立。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Wufeng of Sun Liang of Wu, a great stone at Mount Lili in Yangxian County stood up of itself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Wufeng of Sun Liang of Wu a great stone at Mount Lili in Yangxian County stood up of itself.

sentences.zh: 按京房易傳曰：「庶士為天子之祥也。

translations.literal: Examining the Tradition of Changes of Jing Fang, it says: "The common gentry becoming Son of Heaven is an auspice."
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Tradition of Changes of Jing Fang, it says: "The common gentry becoming Son of Heaven is an auspice."

sentences.zh: 」其說曰：「石立於山，同姓。

translations.literal: Its explanation says: "Stone standing on a mountain—same surname.
translations.idiomatic: Its explanation says: "Stone standing on a mountain—same surname.

sentences.zh: 平地，異姓。

translations.literal: On level ground—different surname."
translations.idiomatic: On level ground—different surname."

sentences.zh: 」干寶以為孫晧承廢故之家得位，其應也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao held that Sun Hao inherited the position from a deposed former house— the corresponding response.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao held that Sun Hao inherited the position from a deposed former house—the corresponding response.

sentences.zh: 或曰孫休見立之祥也。

translations.literal: Some say it was the auspice of Sun Xiu's installation.
translations.idiomatic: Some say it was the auspice of Sun Xiu's installation.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康五年十二月，有石生于宜年里。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, a stone was born in Yinian Lane.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin a stone was born in Yinian Lane.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永康元年，襄陽郡上言得鳴石，撞之，聲聞七八里。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongkang of Emperor Hui of Jin, Xiangyang Commandery reported obtaining a sounding stone; struck, its sound was heard seven or eight li away.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongkang under Emperor Hui of Jin Xiangyang Commandery reported obtaining a sounding stone; struck, its sound was heard seven or eight li away.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝太安元年，丹陽湖熟縣夏架湖有大石浮二百步而登岸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tai'an of Emperor Hui of Jin, at Xiajia Lake in Hushu County of Danyang a great stone floated two hundred paces and came ashore.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tai'an under Emperor Hui of Jin, at Xiajia Lake in Hushu County of Danyang a great stone floated two hundred paces and came ashore.

sentences.zh: 民驚譟相告曰：「石來！

translations.literal: The people cried out in alarm to one another: "The stone is coming!"
translations.idiomatic: The people cried out in alarm to one another: "The stone is coming!"

sentences.zh: 」干寶曰：「尋有石冰入建業。」

translations.literal: Gan Bao says: "Soon afterward Shi Bing entered Jiankang."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao says: "Soon afterward Shi Bing entered Jiankang."

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始八年五月，蜀地雨白毛。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, white hair rained in Shu territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin white hair rained in Shu territory.

sentences.zh: 此白祥也。

translations.literal: This was a white portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was a white portent.

sentences.zh: 是時益州刺史皇甫晏冒暑伐汶山胡，從事何旅固諫，不從。

translations.literal: At this time the Inspector of Yizhou Huangfu Yan braved the heat to campaign against the Wenshan Hu; the Attendant He Lü firmly remonstrated, but he did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Inspector of Yizhou Huangfu Yan braved the heat to campaign against the Wenshan Hu; the Attendant He Lü firmly remonstrated, but he did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 牙門張弘等因眾之怨，誣晏謀逆，害之。

translations.literal: The Gate Officer Zhang Hong and others, exploiting the troops' resentment, falsely accused Yan of plotting rebellion and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Officer Zhang Hong and others, exploiting the troops' resentment, falsely accused Yan of plotting rebellion and killed him.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「前樂後憂，厥妖天雨羽。

translations.literal: The Tradition of Changes of Jing Fang says: "First joy, then sorrow—the anomaly is Heaven raining feathers."
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition of Changes of Jing Fang says: "First joy, then sorrow—the anomaly is Heaven raining feathers."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「邪人進，賢人逃，天雨毛。

translations.literal: It also says: "Evil men advance, worthy men flee—Heaven rains hair."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Evil men advance, worthy men flee—Heaven rains hair."

sentences.zh: 」其易妖曰：「天雨毛羽，貴人出走。

translations.literal: Its Change anomaly says: "Heaven rains hair and feathers—the noble departs in flight."
translations.idiomatic: Its Change anomaly says: "Heaven rains hair and feathers—the noble departs in flight."

sentences.zh: 」三占皆應也。

translations.literal: All three prognostications were fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: All three prognostications were fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永寧元年，齊王冏舉義軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongning of Emperor Hui of Jin, the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong raised a righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongning under Emperor Hui of Jin the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong raised a righteous army.

sentences.zh: 軍中有小兒出於襄城繁昌縣，年八歲，髮體悉白，頗能卜。

translations.literal: In the army there was a child from Fanchang County in Xiangcheng, eight years old, whose hair and body were entirely white and who could divinate fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: In the army there was a child from Fanchang County in Xiangcheng, eight years old, whose hair and body were entirely white and who could divinate fairly well.

sentences.zh: 於洪範，則白祥也。

translations.literal: In the Great Plan, this is a white portent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Great Plan, this is a white portent.

sentences.zh: 晉車騎大將軍東嬴王騰自幷州遷鎮鄴，行次真定。

translations.literal: The Jin General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Dongying Sima Teng, moved from Bing Province to garrison Ye and halted at Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Dongying Sima Teng, moved from Bing Province to garrison Ye and halted at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 時久積雪，而當門前方數尺獨消釋，騰怪而掘之，得玉馬高尺許，口齒缺。

translations.literal: Snow had long accumulated, yet for several chi before the gate alone it melted; Teng found it strange and dug there, obtaining a jade horse about a chi high with broken teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Snow had long accumulated, yet for several chi before the gate alone it melted; Teng found it strange and dug there, obtaining a jade horse about a chi high with broken teeth.

sentences.zh: 騰以馬者國姓，上送之以為瑞。

translations.literal: Teng, since horse is the surname of the state, sent it upward as an auspicious portent.
translations.idiomatic: Teng, since horse is the surname of the state, sent it upward as an auspicious portent.

sentences.zh: 然論者皆云馬而無齒，則不得食，妖祥之兆，衰亡之徵。

translations.literal: Yet commentators all said a horse without teeth cannot eat—an omen of anomaly and auspice, a sign of decline and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet commentators all said a horse without teeth cannot eat—an omen of anomaly and auspice, a sign of decline and ruin.

sentences.zh: 案占，此白祥也。

translations.literal: Examining prognostication, this was a white portent.
translations.idiomatic: Examining prognostication, this was a white portent.

sentences.zh: 是後騰為汲桑所殺，而晉室遂亡。

translations.literal: After this Teng was killed by Ji Sang, and the house of Jin then perished.
translations.idiomatic: After this Teng was killed by Ji Sang, and the house of Jin then perished.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉中，徐湛之為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of Song, Xu Tanzhi was Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of Song Xu Tanzhi was Intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 夜西門內有氣如練，西南指，長數十丈。

translations.literal: At night within the western gate there was vapor like silk, pointing southwest, several tens of zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: At night within the western gate there was vapor like silk, pointing southwest, several tens of zhang long.

sentences.zh: 又白光覆屋，良久而轉駃乃消。

translations.literal: Again white light covered the roof; after a long while it turned swift and then vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Again white light covered the roof; after a long while it turned swift and then vanished.

sentences.zh: 此白祥也。

translations.literal: This was a white portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was a white portent.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和元年，鄧琬在尋陽，種紫花皆白，白眚也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe of the Former Deposed Emperor, Deng Wan was at Xunyang; purple flowers planted all turned white—a white disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe under the Former Deposed Emperor Deng Wan was at Xunyang; purple flowers planted all turned white—a white disaster.

sentences.zh: 木沴金

translations.literal: Wood harms metal
translations.idiomatic: Wood Harms Metal

sentences.zh: 魏齊王正始末，河南尹李勝治聽事，有小材激墮，檛受浮吏石虎斷項之。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengshi of Emperor Qi of Wei, the Intendant of Henan Li Sheng was managing the audience hall; a small timber was struck loose and fell; the mace-bearer Fu Shi Hu severed the neck of the floating clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhengshi of Emperor Qi of Wei the Intendant of Henan Li Sheng was managing the audience hall; a small timber was struck loose and fell; the mace-bearer Fu Shi Hu severed the neck of the floating clerk.

sentences.zh: 此木沴金也。

translations.literal: This was wood harming metal.
translations.idiomatic: This was wood harming metal.

sentences.zh: 勝後旬日而敗。

translations.literal: Sheng was defeated ten days later.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was defeated ten days later.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康八年三月，郊禖壇石中破為二。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, the stone at the suburban Qi altar split in two.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin the stone at the suburban Qi altar split in two.

sentences.zh: 此木沴金也。

translations.literal: This was wood harming metal.
translations.idiomatic: This was wood harming metal.

sentences.zh: 郊禖壇者，求子之神位，無故而自毀，太子將危之妖也。

translations.literal: The suburban Qi altar is the spirit seat for seeking sons; destroyed without cause—it is an omen that the Crown Prince will be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban Qi altar is the spirit seat for seeking sons; destroyed without cause—it is an omen that the Crown Prince will be endangered.

sentences.zh: 明年，愍懷廢死。

translations.literal: The next year Minhuai was deposed and died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Minhuai was deposed and died.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元十年四月，謝安出鎮廣陵，始發石頭，金鼓無故自破。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Xie An went out to govern at Guangling; as he first set out from Shitou, the gongs and drums broke of themselves without cause.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin Xie An went out to govern at Guangling; as he first set out from Shitou, the gongs and drums broke of themselves without cause.

sentences.zh: 此木沴金之異也。

translations.literal: This was an anomaly of wood harming metal.
translations.idiomatic: This was an anomaly of wood harming metal.

sentences.zh: 天意若曰，安徒揚經略之聲，終無其實，鉦鼓不用之象也。

translations.literal: Heaven's intent seems to say: An vainly raises the sound of strategic planning, yet in the end has no substance—the image of gongs and drums unused.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's intent seems to say: An vainly raises the sound of strategic planning, yet in the end has no substance—the image of gongs and drums unused.

sentences.zh: 八月，以疾還，是月薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he returned due to illness; that month he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he returned due to illness; that month he died.
